title: Kummitustarinalle lasten- ja nuortenkirjallisuuden Finlandia-palkinto
content:
Lasten- ja nuortenkirjallisuuden Finlandia-palkinnon on saanut Kristiina Wallinin ja Erika Kallasmaan kummitustarina Älä pelkää, PÖÖ! Voittaja julkistettiin torstai-iltana järjestetyssä palkintojenjakotilaisuudessa.

Kirjassa teksti ja kuva punoutuvat yhteen pienistä kummituksista, kaikenkarvaisista koirista ja hajamietteisistä hahmoista kertovaksi tarinaksi.

Lasten- ja nuortenkirjallisuuden Finlandia-voittajan valitsi Duudsonit-ryhmästä tunnettu Jukka Hildén. Hän kuvaili puheessaan Teoksen kustantamaa voittajakirjaa hauskaksi ja haikeaksi. Kirja kertoo yksinäisyydestä ja pelosta, mutta ei jätä ketään yksin ja antaa rohkeutta.

- Se luottaa lukijaansa ja antaa kuvien kertoa sen, mikä jää rivien väliin. Jäin tuijottamaan kuvia pitkäksi aikaa ja löysin joka kerta jotain uutta, Hildén sanoi perusteluissaan.

HILDÈN kannusti puheessaan ihmisiä lukemaan lapsilleen, sillä lapset ammentavat hänen mukaansa kirjoista arvoja, ymmärrystä, tietoa ja mielikuvitusta. Duudsoni kertoikin lukeneensa kaikki kuusi ehdokaskirjaa ensin yksin ja sitten ääneen.

Hildén kertoi naurun olevan tärkeää, sillä se saa lapsen palaamaan kirjan pariin ja siten ryhtymään lukijaksi.

title: Supporting a progressive digital reform agenda for Bangladesh
content:
To: 
Mr. Tarique Rahman
Honourable Prime Minister
Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh

Subject: supporting a progressive digital reform agenda for Bangladesh

Bangladesh’s digital reforms are at a turning point. We, the undersigned organisations, urge your government to protect what has been achieved, restore the safeguards that have been stripped away, and build a legal and institutional framework that centres people’s rights, democratic accountability, and a free, open and secure internet.

Digital reform is an essential part of delivering on your stated commitment to strengthen accountability and prevent authoritarianism. Laws and institutions governing online expression,  privacy, cybersecurity, surveillance and artificial intelligence shape how people participate in public life, access services, organise, communicate and hold power to account.

title: No conditions for life: Women, girls and the gendered dimensions of Israel’s genocide against Palestinians in Gaza – Report Launch, 25 November 2026 – Introductory Speech
content:
Dear colleagues and friends,

Thank you for joining us from around the world for the launch of our latest report on Gaza, No conditions for life: Women, girls and the gendered dimensions of Israel’s genocide against Palestinians in Gaza, which comes two years after we concluded unequivocally that Israel was committing genocide against Palestinians in the occupied Gaza Strip.

Thank you to all the Media present and others, for listening and reporting on the senseless killings and the victims, on how Palestinian organizations, Amnesty and other international organizations, the Special Rapporteur and the UN Commission of Inquiry and others have bravely urged the international community to protect Palestinians in Gaza from genocide and those in the West Bank from ethnic cleansing, despite the sanctions imposed on some, the threats on others, along with the propaganda and vicious silencing.

title: "I'm Not Going to Give Up": Leonard Peltier on Indigenous Rights, His Half-Century in Prison & Coming Home
content:
In September 2025, Democracy Now! host Amy Goodman sat down with longtime political prisoner and Indigenous activist Leonard Peltier for his first extended television and radio broadcast interview since his release to home confinement in February 2025. Before his commutation by former President Joe Biden, the 82-year-old Peltier spent nearly 50 years behind bars. Peltier has always maintained his innocence for the 1975 killing of two FBI officers. He is expected to serve the remainder of his life sentences under house arrest at the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Nation in Belcourt, North Dakota. In a wide-ranging conversation, we spoke to Peltier about his case, his time in prison, his childhood spent at an American Indian boarding school and his later involvement in the American Indian Movement (AIM) and more.

“We still have to live under that, that fear of losing our identity, losing our culture, our religion,” Peltier says about his continued commitment to Indigenous rights. “The struggle still goes on for me. I’m not going to give up.”

title: Toistaminen ei tee väärästä väitteestä totta
content:
Lähes kaikki oppositiopuolueet haluavat perua yhteisöveron alennuksen. Peruminen ei kuitenkaan lisää verotuloja 840 miljoonalla, vaikka niin toistellaan. Sen takaavat veroalen lisäämät investoinnit ja ennen kaikkea työn korkea verokiila. Veroalen muut vaikutuskanavat tuskin kumoavat näitä hyötyjä julkiselle taloudelle, koska työttömiä löytyy, maahanmuutto on mahdollista ja kannustinloukkuja on purettu, kirjoittaa Etla-kolumnissaan Aki Kangasharju.

Yhteisöveron alennuksen staattisesta 840 miljoonan euron verovaikutuksesta on tullut mantra, jota toistelevat oppositiopuolueet vaaliohjelmissaan ja vaihtoehtobudjeteissaan. Arvio on kuitenkin varmasti väärä, sillä yhteisöveron lasku kasvattaa kiistatta yhteisöveron pohjaa (veronalaisia voittoja).

Uudet yhteisöverotulot eivät tosin kata kokonaan staattista verotulomenetystä, mutta kattavat kuitenkin suurella varmuudella osan.

Lisäksi veron alentaminen vaikuttaa muuhunkin talouteen. Sitä ei tunnisteta, vaikka erityisesti Suomen kaltaisessa korkean työn verotuksen maassa verotulot kasvavat voimakkaasti aina, kun veroale lisää työllisyyttä.

title: New UN Report Investigates Attacks on Aid Workers During Sri Lanka’s Civil War
content:
On August 4, 2006, 17 Sri Lankan staff members of the Paris-based humanitarian organization Action Contre la Faim (Action Against Hunger) were summarily executed at their office in Muttur, Sri Lanka. Over 20 years later, this unresolved case is emblematic of attacks on humanitarian workers during the country’s brutal civil war that ended in 2009.

A new report by the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, “I Died Many Times”; Attacks on Humanitarian Assistance in Sri Lanka, documents the numerous threats aid workers faced during the final years of Sri Lanka’s civil war with the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam.

The report finds that the government purposefully shut down humanitarian space “as a slow, deliberate strangulation” that effectively cordoned civilians into government-held areas, preventing independent observers from witnessing war crimes by the warring parties. The report, which is the latest from the UN’s Sri Lanka Accountability Project to gather evidence of international crimes in Sri Lanka, also finds “that impunity has resulted not from isolated failures, but from mutually reinforcing practices that have repeatedly frustrated accountability.”

title: Right-Wing Influencer Involved in ‘Reckless’ Release of USAID Files
content:
A right-wing influencer who briefly worked at the U.S. State Department appears to have orchestrated the release of more than a gigabyte of private communications and internal documents from USAID, the defunct U.S. foreign aid agency.

The files appear on USAID’s official website, which had been shut down after the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump ended most U.S. foreign assistance in the summer of 2025.

Its relaunch was announced on the social media platform X this Wednesday by Mike Benz, a self-styled free speech advocate and censorship researcher who has long campaigned against USAID’s alleged role in online censorship and manipulation.

Benz, who has 1.1 million followers on X, was a key voice urging on the Trump administration’s efforts last year to end most U.S. foreign assistance. He was reportedly hired as a special government employee last December in order to dig through USAID’s archives. (The State Department did not answer questions from OCCRP on whether Benz is an employee.)

title: How a Thanksgiving Crisis Inspired the Invention of Swanson’s TV Dinner (1953)
content:
“Taste — the mouth’s response to the sensation of eating and drinking — is a strange and complex and complicated thing,” writes New York Times food editor Craig Claiborne. “I am convinced that there are a multitude of people (Americans, mostly, to judge by the people who buy TV dinners and frozen pizzas) who have no taste whatsoever.” That column was published almost exactly 50 years ago, but even at that point, such convenience-oriented food products had already enjoyed prominence in American life for two decades. Though it could hardly have made a dent in the popularity of TV dinners, Claiborne’s typically waspish aside did draw a letter of objection from one Rosalie Levine of Lakewood, California.

“I live alone, I must control my weight. I am not a skilled cook,” she writes. The TV dinner’s price “cannot possibly be bettered”; what’s more, “each oven-ready dinner takes only half an hour’s worth of gas to prepare, and there are no pots or pans to clean up afterward.” While none of these advantages were accidental, the oft-told story of the concept’s emergence begins with a corporate crisis.

title: EU leaders brave clash with Trump over tech tax, defense, Ukraine
content:
BRUSSELS ― EU leaders are warming to the idea of a possible fight with U.S. President Donald Trump over everything from digital taxes to defense procurement rules and financing for Ukraine.

As tense talks on the EU’s long-term budget descended into political theatrics on Thursday night, leaders including French President Emmanuel Macron continued to push for these measures.

“France defends this [digital tax] idea and has done so since 2018,” Macron told reporters. Europe was “very legitimate” in imposing such a levy because the U.S. wasn’t respecting international tax agreements agreed by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, he added.

Such proposals put Brussels on a collision course with Washington, which has repeatedly railed against policies that are seen as discriminating against U.S. interests. Trump has also taken issue with Europe’s continued support for Ukraine, just as leaders prepare to sign off on a €45 billion loan for Kyiv before the end of this year.

title: Paula Huotelin valittiin arkkitehtien maailmanjärjestön UIA:n varapuheenjohtajaksi
content:
Arkkitehtien maailmanjärjestö UIA (Union Internationale des Architectes) edustaa yli 100 maan kansallista arkkitehtijärjestöä ja niiden kautta yli miljoonaa arkkitehtia. Järjestön päämaja on Pariisissa. Puheenjohtajan lisäksi sillä on viisi alueellista varapuheenjohtajaa, joista Paula Huotelin vastaa Euroopan alueesta.

Hän on toiminut aiemmin UIA:n luottamustehtävissä, muun muassa neuvoston jäsenenä ja kilpailukomission toisena johtajana. Hän on UIA:n kolmas suomalainen varapuheenjohtaja.

“Paula Huotelin on sujuvasti laajentanut ja vahvistanut SAFAn rajat ylittäviä yhteyksiä. Hänen kansainvälisissä tehtävissä saavuttamansa arvostus näkyi myös kesällä Barcelonassa UIA:n maailmankongressin tapahtumissa ja keskusteluissa”, SAFAn puheenjohtaja Asko Takala sanoo.

Huotelin edustaa UIA:ssa Pohjoismaiden jäsenosastoa.

“Pohjoismaisten liittojen yhteisen ryhmittymän oli – monen muun maan edustajien kannustamana – luontevaa asettaa Paula ehdolle tähän toimeen.”

Paula Huotelin painottaa, että järjestötyössä kaikkien jäsenten äänen on kuuluttava ja että vertaisoppiminen on kansainvälisen yhteistyön ytimessä.

title: Westermarckutgåvan växer med nya brev och artiklar
content:
Den digitala utgåvan Brev, artiklar och fältstudier har utökats med 480 brev och 25 akademiska artiklar. Det nypublicerade materialet breddar bilden av Edvard Westermarcks forskning, vänskapsrelationer och samtid.

Bland nyheterna på westermarck.sls.fi finns den omfattande korrespondensen med vännen och professorn i filosofi Rolf Lagerborg, som nu har kompletterats och publicerats i sin helhet. De 330 nytillkomna breven ger inblickar i forskning, universitetslivet samt politiska och sociala skeenden, men också i den nära relationen mellan två av sin tids mest framstående finländska intellektuella.

Dessutom har en tidigare opublicerad brevväxling med språkvetaren, professorn och samhällsdebattören Julio Reuter lagts till i utgåvan. De omkring 150 breven berör bland annat det passiva motståndet mot det ryska styret, kulturadressen Pro Finlandia och andra aktuella frågor i det finländska samhället kring sekelskiftet 1900.

Bland det nypublicerade materialet finns också 25 antropologiska artiklar av Westermarck från Geografiska Föreningens Tidskrift, Nutid, Folklore, Sociological Papers och Revue internationale de sociologie.

Den digitala utgåvan utökas kontinuerligt

title: "Sodan hintaa maksaa myös luonto"– brittiuimari ui Hormuzinsalmessa
content:
Konfliktien aiheuttamat ympäristövahingot saavat usein vähemmän huomiota kuin inhimilliset kustannukset. YK:n mertensuojelun lähetti, brittiläinen kestävyysuimari Lewis Pugh ui Hormuzinsalmen poikki herättääkseen huomiota iskujen aiheuttamille öljyvuodoille ja muulle saastumiselle, kirjoittaa The Guardian. Hyökkäyksillä voi olla pitkäaikaisia seurauksia meriekosysteemeille, kuten koralliriutoille, meriheinäniityille ja mangrovemetsille.

Hormuzinsalmen konflikti alkoi lähes yhdeksän kuukautta sitten, eikä Iranin ja Yhdysvaltojen rauha siinnä vieläkään näköpiirissä. Persian- ja Omaninlahdet erottava salmi on keskeinen reitti Lähi-idän öljykuljetuksille.

56-vuotias Lewis Pugh todisti kolmipäiväisen uintinsa aikana useita hyökkäyksiä kauppa-aluksia vastaan, hävittäjiä yläpuolellaan sekä kaukaisempia räjähdyksiä, Guardianissa kirjoitetaan. Hän taittoi salmessa noin 15 kilometrin matkan. Pieneen retkikuntaan kuuluivat tukivene ja kajakki, jotka pysyttelivät Pughin rinnalla koko ajan.

title: ATO 2026: Is Open Source Dying? Short film and open discussion
content:
In October, the OSI hosted the State of the Source track at All Things Open designed to connect developers with the big policy conversations shaping our ecosystem. Jonathan Starr, Executive Director of the Open Source Endowment, led “Is Open Source Dying? Short film and open discussion.”

The idea that AI could end Open Source is provocative, but it distracts from the real issue: sustainability. This short film and open discussion explores how foundations, funding platforms, grants, and corporate contributions can evolve to support maintainers and build a more resilient Open Source ecosystem in the age of AI.

Nick Vidal: All right. So, the title of this session, “Saving Open Source in the Era of AI,” is kind of provocative, right? I mean, is AI going to be killing open source or is it going to help? So, in your view, Jonathan, what are we actually trying to save?

title: Blogi: Koheesio on myös geopoliittinen aihe: Miksi lisää EU-budjettisolidaarisuutta on Suomen etu
content:
Kirjoitus on julkaistu alunperin kirjoittajan toimittamassa “Der (europäische) Föderalist” -blogissa ja on luettavissa täällä.

Neuvottelut EU:n seuraavasta pitkän aikavälin talousarviosta ovat saavuttaneet ratkaisevan vaiheen. Tämä on johtanut tavanomaiseen, lähes rituaalimaiseen ryhmämuodostukseen: Euroopan komissio ja Euroopan parlamentti haluavat suuremman budjetin, jotta EU voisi hoitaa kasvavat velvollisuutensa. ”Nuukat” maat haluavat estää kaikenlaiset korotukset, jotta heidän ei tarvitsisi maksaa enemmän. ”Koheesion ystävät” haluavat säilyttää maksut taloudellisesti heikommille jäsenvaltioille ja alueille. Maat, joilla on merkittävä maataloussektori, haluavat estää maatalouspolitiikan leikkaukset. Jotkut jäsenvaltiot haluavat myös lisätä investointeja uusiin painopistealueisiin, kuten puolustukseen.

Entä Suomi?

EU:n budjetin nettomaksajana Suomen hallitus on vaistomaisesti asettunut nuukien leiriin. Syyskuun lopussa pääministeri Petteri Orpo (Kok./EPP) allekirjoitti yhteisen kirjeen Saksan, Itävallan, Alankomaiden, Ruotsin ja Tanskan hallitusten johtajien kanssa, jossa vaadittiin budjettiesityksen leikkaamista ”satojen miljardien eurojen” verran.

title: Women Wiki camp in Southeast Serbia
content:
Between April and October 2026, Wikimedia Serbia ran Digital Voices of Southeast Serbia, a project supported by the CIVICUS Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI), aimed at closing both the gender and regional knowledge gaps on Wikipedia. By combining local research with an in-person mentorship camp in Pirot, the project helped women from southeastern Serbia overcome the fear of online judgment and publish 41 new articles on Serbian Wikipedia, with two participants now stepping up to lead their own Wikimedia grant project next year.

Before organizing any events, we wanted to understand what actually stops women in southeast Serbia from contributing online. We conducted a survey with 100 women across the region to map their digital habits and barriers.

The results were revealing:

  • 100% of respondents use the internet every day.
  • 94% act strictly as passive consumers—reading content, but never writing or editing online.
  • Over 86% stated that fear of online attacks, harsh criticism, and judgment from their local, more conservative communities stops them from creating digital content.

title: RoboArena
content:
Humanoide Roboter laufen, tanzen, greifen nach Gegenständen und bewegen sich erstaunlich menschenähnlich. Doch was steckt hinter diesen Fähigkeiten? Warum werden Maschinen überhaupt mit zwei Armen, zwei Beinen und einem Kopf ausgestattet? Sollen sie uns im Alltag unterstützen, gefährliche Arbeiten übernehmen oder vor allem faszinieren und unterhalten?

Noch folgen die meisten Roboter vorgegebenen Abläufen. Die Zukunft der Robotik könnte jedoch eng mit künstlicher Intelligenz verbunden sein: Maschinen, die ihre Umgebung selbstständig wahrnehmen, aus Erfahrungen lernen und flexibel auf neue Situationen reagieren. Was würde es bedeuten, wenn Roboter tatsächlich eigenständig handeln könnten? Welche Risiken und Befürchtungen weckt die Vorstellung autonomer Maschinen? Und welchen tatsächlichen Mehrwert könnten sie für die Gesellschaft bringen? 
Gerade bei humanoiden Robotern stellt sich die Frage, welchen konkreten Nutzen ihre menschenähnliche Gestalt hat – und ob sie tatsächlich für jene Aufgaben geeignet sind, für die sie entwickelt und mit großem Aufwand vermarktet werden.

title: Czechia changes rules for social media. But its implementation of the DSA may conflict with EU law
content:
Social media platforms, online marketplaces and search engines all fall under the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA), which imposes a range of obligations on them. These include making it easier for users to report illegal content, ensuring greater transparency in content moderation and allowing users to appeal certain decisions made by platforms.

Czechia’s Digital Economy Act sets out how compliance with the EU regulation will be monitored and enforced at national level. Czech MPs approved the legislation recently. Its provisions changed several times during the drafting process, both during consultations with experts and as a result of amendments proposed by MPs.

The Czech Telecommunications Office (CTO) will play a key role in overseeing compliance with the DSA, becoming the country’s Digital Services Coordinator. The Chamber of Deputies also added a provision requiring supervisory authorities to take freedom of expression and the right to access information into account when making decisions.

title: Sinking islands or green Titanic? COP31 failure splits Parliament
content:
For the first time since 2009, a UN climate summit ended without a deal. In the European Parliament, the collapse of COP31 in Antalya has exposed a deep rift. Some lawmakers want Europe to fight harder for the climate. Others see the failure as proof that the EU should scale back its targets.

“Here we are, talking about words in an agreement, while on the other side of the world, islands are disappearing under water.” With these words, MEP Ingeborg ter Laak (EPP/NLD) captured the frustration expressed by several lawmakers during the debate on Thursday (26 November) on the outcome of COP31. She compared a climate agreement that makes no mention of fossil fuels to an attempt to extinguish a fire without first shutting off its fuel supply.

MEP Mohammed Chahim (S&D/NLD) was equally critical of the summit’s outcome. “History will remember this summit. Not for what they achieved, but for what they refused to do,” Mr Chahim said.

title: Europe has bought two years on methane – now it must use them
content: Europe has learned the hard way what energy insecurity costs. First came the price shock after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine; then, this year, the disruption around the Strait of Hormuz has pushed bills up again. For households stretched by the cost of living, the price of energy decides whether or not they can heat their homes. Yet there is a quieter waste of energy: every year, around 200 billion cubic metres of gas, roughly two-thirds of total annual EU gas consumption, leaks, is vented or is burned off during the world’s oil and gas operations.

title: Can the International Criminal Court survive Trump’s attacks – and hold world leaders to account?
content:
More than eight years after Rodrigo Duterte announced the Philippines would withdraw from the International Criminal Court (ICC), the country’s former president is about to begin his trial in The Hague.

Duterte faces charges of crimes against humanity over alleged killings carried out during his deadly war on drugs.

The trial, which begins on 30 November, comes at a precarious moment for the court, as the United States ramps up its efforts to undermine the institution.

“Nothing has really quite approached this level of hostility we’re seeing coming from President Trump, or more particularly Marco Rubio,” explains Carrie McDougall, an associate professor at Melbourne Law School, speaking on The Conversation Weekly podcast.

The US has never joined the ICC, citing concerns about politically motivated prosecutions of its nationals. But the court can investigate alleged war crimes committed by Americans on the territory of its member countries.

McDougall says the US has “made no bones” about its opposition to the investigation of US nationals and the prosecution of Israeli nationals.

title: Tietokirjallisuuden Finlandia-palkinto jaettu – ”Kyllä se tavallaan lähti vähän lapasesta ja karkasi käsistä”
content:
Kun Elias Lönnrot vuonna 1863 suomensi Johan Philip Palménin teosta Lainopillinen käsikirja: Yhteiseksi sivistykseksi, hän käänsi ruotsinkielisen käsitteen välfärdspoliti suomeksi termillä onnivallinto.

Sillä tarkoitettiin toimintaa, jonka tavoitteena oli huolehtia väestön elinoloista ja edistää kansalaisten turvallisuutta ja toimeentuloa.

Lönnrot siis puhui jo pitkälle toista sataa vuotta sitten hyvinvointivaltiosta.

Sen jälkeen puhetta on aiheesta riittänytkin. Milloin mitäkin on yritetty joko oikeuttaa tai karsia sillä perusteella, että hyvinvointivaltiotahan tässä ollaan ylläpitämässä. Hämäräksi on usein jäänyt, mistä oikein puhutaan, kun puhutaan hyvinvointivaltiosta.

Tuoreet Finladia-voittajat Antti Karisto ja Jussi Simpura tulevat apuun teoksellaan Hyvinvoinnin historiaa – Ajankuvia Suomesta. Kirja kattaa yli sadan vuoden jatkumon suomalaisesta hyvin- ja pahoinvoinnista 1910-luvulta aina nykypäivään saakka. Urakka on valtava ja kirja paksu, yli 320 sivua ja toista sataa sivua lähde- ja kirjallisuusviitteitä.

title: Philippines: Duterte trial a defining test for justice, accountability and future of the ICC
content:
Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte’s trial at the International Criminal Court (ICC) for crimes against humanity is a historic opportunity for justice for victims of the so-called “war on drugs” and a defining test for the future of international accountability, Amnesty International said ahead of the trial starting on Monday 30 November.

The trial, which will focus on murders and attempted murders allegedly committed between 2013 and 2019 while Duterte was President of the Philippines and Mayor of Davao City, opens at a time when the ICC is facing unprecedented attacks from the US government and other powerful states.

“For thousands of families of victims, this trial represents something they have been denied for years: the chance to see those allegedly responsible for horrific crimes brought before a court of law,” said Ritz Lee Santos III, Executive Director of Amnesty International Philippines.

“The victims and survivors of the so-called ‘war on drugs’ have shown extraordinary courage and determination in pursuing justice. They must remain at the centre of these proceedings every step of the way.”

title: The proposed EU Quantum Act: from quantum readiness to industrial capacity
content:
The European Commission’s proposal for a Quantum Act brings Europe’s quantum ambitions into sharper focus. For businesses, it combines opportunities to commercialise quantum technologies with a renewed imperative to prepare for their security implications.

In our earlier article on Quantum Transition, we explained why organisations should begin preparing for the quantum transition before the regulatory framework catches up. The Commission’s proposal of 25 November 2026 marks a new step: a proposed Quantum Act aims to strengthen the European Union’s competitiveness and resilience in the global quantum ecosystem. Its more specific objectives are to translate research strengths into products and services, strengthen supply chains and support the transition to post-quantum cryptography. It also lays the groundwork for a Sovereign Tech Equity Fund (STEF). The message for businesses remains unchanged: legislative developments should inform, not postpone, preparedness. 1

title: ICC: Promote, Protect International Justice
content:
(The Hague) – Member countries of the International Criminal Court (ICC) should prioritize measures to promote and protect the court and those cooperating with it, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today. The 24-page report makes detailed recommendations for the annual session of the ICC’s Assembly of States Parties, which will convene in The Hague from November 30 to December 7, 2026.

This year’s session takes place as the court and the broader international justice system face unrelenting pressure from the United States. On October 9, the US government escalated its campaign to destroy the ICC “brick by brick” by imposing sanctions on the whole court under a February 2025 executive order. This followed the sanctioning of ICC judges and prosecutors, a United Nations human rights expert, and three leading Palestinian rights organizations. Yet, the ICC continues to advance its critical work for justice. The landmark trial of former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte is scheduled to begin on November 30.

title: The Illustrated Version of “Alice’s Restaurant”: Watch Arlo Guthrie’s Thanksgiving Counterculture Classic
content: Alice’s Restaurant. It’s now a Thanksgiving classic, and something of a tradition around here. Recorded in 1967, the 18+ minute counterculture song recounts Arlo Guthrie’s real encounter with the law, starting on Thanksgiving Day 1965. As the long song unfolds, we hear all about how a hippie-bating police officer, by the name of William “Obie” Obanhein, arrested Arlo for littering. (Cultural footnote: Obie previously posed for several Norman Rockwell paintings, including the well-known painting, “The Runaway,” that graced a 1958 cover of The Saturday Evening Post.) In fairly short order, Arlo pleads guilty to a misdemeanor charge, pays a $25 fine, and cleans up the thrash. But the story isn’t over. Not by a long shot.

title: US warns EU leaders against Big Tech tax
content:
BRUSSELS — The Trump administration is warning EU leaders against taxing Big Tech as they gather in Brussels to consider new options to fund the bloc’s next budget. 

“We oppose the EU proposal for an EU-wide digital levy just as we have opposed (and continue to oppose) other digital services taxes that discriminate against US companies while hurting consumers as well,” a spokesperson for the U.S. State Department told POLITICO in a statement, reiterating Washington’s years-long opposition.  

European Council President António Costa on Saturday proposed reviving talks on a European digital tax to help finance the EU’s €2 trillion long-term budget and unlock a deal on its final size. 

It would target companies with global turnover above €750 million, including at least €50 million in Europe — a threshold that would catch U.S. tech giants such as Google, Meta and Amazon. 

The warning came as EU leaders opened a two-day extraordinary summit in Brussels on Thursday to grapple with the next budget’s complex funding equation: how much to spend and how to reduce the burden on national coffers by raising new revenue through so-called “own resources.”

title: Ett nytt förbund för samman Finlands arkivsektor
content:
Det stiftande mötet för Finlands arkivförbund hölls den 23 november 2026 i Helsingfors.

De centrala aktörerna inom arkivsektorn har grundat Finlands arkivförbund, vars uppgift blir att bevaka arkivsektorns intressen, koordinera samarbete och kommunikation, erbjuda fortbildning för arkivpersonal och främja nätverkande inom sektorn. Finlands arkivförbund kommer även att erbjuda juridisk rådgivning

Planer på att grunda ett arkivförbund har funnits en längre tid, men i fjol beslutade ett flertal centrala aktörer inom arkivsektorn att gå vidare med etableringen av en riksomfattande organisation.

– Finland har saknat en samlande aktör för arkivfältet, som för samman organisationerna inom branschen och driver frågor som är gemensamma för arkivsektorn nationellt, säger Finska Litteratursällskapets arkivchef Outi Hupaniittu.

Arkiven utgör nationens minne. För närvarande påverkas arkivens verksamhet särskilt av den snabba AI-utvecklingen och av det instabila världspolitiska läget.

title: UN sacked Palestinian staff on back of unproven Israeli allegations, tribunal rules
content:
Judgment casts doubt on evidence linking aid workers to Hamas and says humanitarian efforts in Gaza were damaged

A UN tribunal has cast doubt on the evidence used to justify the sacking of Palestinian UN aid workers in 2024, saying it was based “almost entirely” on unproven assertions from the Israeli government and had damaged humanitarian operations in Gaza.

The judgment, seen by the Guardian, raises fresh questions about the decision by the UN Relief and Works Agency (Unrwa), the main humanitarian organisation working in Gaza, to sack members of staff. It was taken on the basis of Israeli allegations of involvement in the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023.

title: A Decade of Tulu Wikipedia: Celebrating 10 Years of Community, Culture and Open Knowledge
content:
2008 — Tulu Wikipedia begins as an Incubator project under the Wikimedia Foundation.

2016 — Officially launched as a full Wikipedia project ( 23rd Indian-language Wikipedia) on 6 August 2016 during WikiConference India 2016, Chandigarh.

2026 — Completed a decade of documenting Tulu knowledge on 06 August 2026 in Mangaluru.

From an eight-year journey in the Wikimedia Incubator to a thriving digital knowledge platform with more than 4,000 articles, Tulu Wikipedia’s tenth anniversary celebrated the power of volunteerism, regional collaboration and the preservation of a living language.

In September 2026, the Tulu Wikimedia community came together in Mangaluru, Karnataka, to celebrate a remarkable milestone: ten years of Tulu Wikipedia as a live Wikipedia edition. Held on September 12–13 at A J Grand Hotel, the two-day decennial celebration brought together more than 65 participants, including Wikimedians, students, educators, researchers, language enthusiasts, family members and cultural practitioners.

title: Game over for Temu’s sales tactics? Brussels pushes a reset
content:
Spin a wheel to get in, rush because stock is ‘almost sold out’, and trust a review that may be fake. EU consumer authorities say that was shopping on Temu. Now, under pressure from regulators, the platform has promised to change course.

Temu reaches around 124 million people in the EU every month, by its own count, although it only arrived in April 2023. It rides a wave of cheap online shopping. Almost 6bn low-value parcels entered the EU in 2025, most of them from China, according to Commission data. That growth has put the platform firmly in the sights of EU regulators.

On 26 November, the Consumer Protection Cooperation (CPC) Network of national consumer authorities accepted Temu’s commitments to change practices that, in the Commission’s words, “mislead consumers or unduly influence their purchasing decisions”. Belgium, Germany, and Ireland, home to Temu’s European headquarters, led the case, while the European Commission coordinated it.

title: Turning Europe’s carbon market into an engine for clean investment
content:
The ongoing reform of the EU’s emissions trading system is an opportunity to reposition this cornerstone climate policy instrument into a driver of investments into decarbonised processes and value chains. This requires rethinking the ETS and embedding it firmly into Europe’s industrial policy – by earmarking auction revenue to support decarbonisation investment, restricting free allowances to those willing to invest, and ensuring the carbon price is sufficient so that clean investment pays off.

In its first 20 years, the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) brought the sectors it covers – energy, heavy industry and aviation – halfway to climate neutrality. As the centrepiece of EU climate policy, it serves to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in a market-based and cost-effective way. So far, most of these reductions have come from the energy sector, mainly by phasing out coal, helped by the growing share of renewable power generation.

title: Is Russia about to launch a nuclear weapon into Earth’s orbit? A space law expert explains the threat
content:
As early as December. That’s how soon Russia could put a satellite carrying a nuclear weapon in orbit, according to German media reports.

If the news sounds familiar from headlines past, that’s because it is. In 2024, the United States made a similar allegation, albeit without giving any potential launch window.

These latest reports claim that the satellite, Sputnik-S, was assembled several years ago and is in storage near Moscow.

Intelligence agencies in NATO countries have reportedly shared information about the satellite. This week, the alliance’s secretary general asserted that protecting NATO territory includes keeping it safe from threats to space systems.

Russia’s embassy in Berlin said it “categorically reject[s] all these groundless allegations”. Echoing Moscow’s 2024 denial, it called the reports “propaganda”, adding that Russia “strictly adheres to the fundamental 1967 Outer Space Treaty”.

What is this treaty and what does it say about nuclear weapons? And how could the international community respond or even verify what is on board a satellite?

The prospect of nuclear weapons off-Earth helped drive negotiations for the treaty invoked by Russia.

title: All the Worst Government GTA Memes from Around the World
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a true monocultural event. Every news channel is covering it, anyone with a passing interest in video games is playing it, and it’s made almost $4 billion in less than a week. Desperate to connect with constituents, governments around the world have tried to capitalize on GTA’s popularity by releasing some of the worst AI-generated memes I’ve ever seen. The pictures of politicians in the hyper-real cartoon pink-tinted style of GTA 6 are so awful they even caused a minor political scandal in Scotland.

Let’s begin in the United States, where Vice President JD Vance, the White House, and several other government-run X accounts attempted to capture the cultural zeitgeist by quickly churning out AI-generated meme garbage. GTA has long been popular with Trump 2.0 officials. In March, the official X account of the White House published a compilation of strikes on Iranian targets overlaid with the “WASTED” game over screen from GTA.

title: Sri Lanka: UN report underscores need to end decades-long impunity for conflict-related crimes
content:
Responding to the publication of a new report by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) on crimes under international law committed during Sri Lanka’s 25-year internal armed conflict, Smriti Singh, Amnesty International’s South Asia Director, said:  

“This report shines a light on the fact that no progress has been made in addressing crimes under international law in Sri Lanka and that truth, justice and reparation remain elusive for hundreds and thousands of victims. Its findings reflect the unwillingness of successive Sri Lankan governments to investigate allegations and ensure accountability for abuses committed during the internal armed conflict that ended in 2009. Impunity persists even as mass graves continue to be identified, such as in Chemmani where recent exhumations found the remains of more than 583 individuals, including children.

title: Vaurauden keskittyminen ruokkii ylikulutusta – tutkijat esittävät varallisuusveroa
content:
Nykyinen kansainvälinen verojärjestelmä suosii suhteettomasti kaikkein varakkaimpia ja vaikeuttaa heidän varallisuutensa tehokasta verottamista. Suuret tuloerot ja erityisesti liian suuret varallisuuserot ovat yksi kestävyysmurroksen ydinongelmista siksi, että yksilöiden ja kotitalouksien ympäristöjalanjälki on suoraan yhteydessä niiden tulo- ja varallisuustasoon.

"Ylikulutus ja köyhyys kumpuavat samoista taloudellisista rakenteista, jotka keskittävät vaurautta ja valtaa yhä harvemmille. Eniten ansaitseva 10 % on keskeisessä vastuussa maapallon rajojen ylittämisestä. Myös suuri osa suomalaisista kuuluu tähän tuloluokkaan, jonka kulutuksesta aiheutuvien ympäristövahinkojen kustannusten on arvioitu olevan useita prosentteja maailman bruttokansantuotteesta", Kestävyyspaneelin puheenjohtaja, LUT-yliopiston ympäristötalouden professori Lassi Linnanen sanoo.

Esimerkiksi tekoälyyn tehtävät miljardiluokan investoinnit ovat ajankohtainen esimerkki kiihtyvästä varallisuuden keskittymisestä. Kun teknologialla korvataan ihmistyötä, tulot siirtyvät palkoista pääoman tuotoiksi: työstä kertyvä veropohja kaventuu samalla, kun tekoäly-yritysten voitot kasvavat. Näin osa työpaikoista katoaa ja yhä suurempi osa taloudellisesta arvosta kertyy teknologian omistajille sen sijaan, että se jakautuisi palkkoina työntekijöille.

Varallisuuden keskittymistä voidaan hillitä vain useilla toisiaan tukevilla politiikkatoimilla. Yhtenä politiikkasuosituksena Kestävyyspaneeli esittää varallisuuteen kohdistuvaa veroa, joka huomioisi myös omistusten arvonnousun kautta kertyvän vaurauden. Kansainvälisessä keskustelussa vastaavaa mallia on kutsuttu muun muassa miljardööriveroksi. Suomessa varallisuusvero poistettiin vuonna 2006.

title: Germany: Funding Cuts Threaten Anti-Discrimination Efforts
content:
(Berlin, November 26, 2026) – The German government’s decision to discontinue funding for dozens of civil society projects, following budget cuts, undermines Germany’s efforts to address racism, discrimination, and antisemitism and protect human rights, Human Rights Watch said today. The German government and Bundestag should release further funds to guarantee the continuation of dozens of essential civil society projects. The Bundestag is due to vote on the federal budget on November 27, 2026.

“The German government’s cuts undermine critical civil society work and networks that directly protect human rights and combat the threats from the far-right,” said Almaz Teffera, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch. “The German government and Bundestag should remedy the cuts in the federal budget by providing funds to save trusted anti-discrimination and anti-extremism work that directly protects and empowers people at this critical time.”

title: Study shows stark differences in how much EU countries depend on US Big Tech
content:
BRUSSELS — Even if the EU is united in its resolve to reduce reliance on U.S. technology, each country will have to unplug on its own — and some will have far more unplugging to do than others.

A study by researchers in Finland has found a significant disparity in how much European governments rely on Amazon, Microsoft and Google for digital services aimed at citizens.

“This variation is not random, it’s systematic,” said Vili Lehdonvirta, a professor of technology policy at Finland’s Aalto University and co-author of the report, which comes out as the EU seeks to improve “digital sovereignty” among its 27 member countries.

The researchers studied government websites across 158 countries — including portals where people can find information, submit applications and handle administrative tasks — to estimate how much they depend on the three U.S. Big Tech players.

In the EU, Malta, Finland and Ireland have the highest estimated shares of national public services hosted by U.S. hyperscalers: 78.5%, 56.1% and 45.8%, respectively.

In contrast, France’s estimate is 9.3%, compared with Germany’s 2.9%.

title: Parliament passes medicine reforms, but drug prices stay with capitals
content:
Shortages and long waits for new medicines are what Europe’s biggest pharma reform in 20 years is meant to fix. Parliament approved it on Wednesday, together with the Critical Medicines Act. But the new laws leave drug prices with national capitals, just as pressure from US pricing grows.

In a plenary session on Thursday, MEPs urged the European Commission to stop member states from making their own deals with Washington. “Divided, we take the price. United, we set the terms,” said Stine Bosse (Renew/DNK).

They also asked what the Commission will do now. Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, answered for the Commission. She did not say. Pricing stays with the member states, she said. She asked Parliament to pass the Biotech Act “as soon as possible”.

The debate came one day after Parliament gave final approval to the pharma package and the Critical Medicines Act (CMA). It followed a question to the Commission from Ms Bosse, on behalf of Parliament’s Committee on Public Health (SANT).

title: The dentist won't be seeing you now
content: Got a toothache? Tough luck. Across much of Europe, dental care comes out of your own pocket. Around 10 million people in the EU skipped dental care in 2025, according to Eurostat data, mostly because of cost. People are four times more likely to skip the dentist where they pay most of the bill. Public healthcare schemes only cover about a third of dental spending in the EU. Germany, France, and Croatia are the exceptions, covering more than 60%. But more money isn't a magic fix. In Denmark, the state’s share of dental spending has held stable at around a third since 2010, yet the share of Danes skipping the dentist because of cost rose from 1.2% to 7.8%. The government now pledges to make dental care free within the next decade. Across 22 countries, more public money for dental care since 2008 didn't mean fewer people skipped the dentist over cost. What could help is making sure that money actually reaches those who need it. In 2025, 5.5% of the EU's poorest adults skipped dental care because of cost, versus less than 1% of the richest. Since 2008, the share of people unable to afford dental care has fallen by 30%. But for many, a trip to the dentist is still a luxury.

title: Using AI to hunt for Black Friday bargains? That ‘great deal’ might not exist
content:
To get the most out of Black Friday sales, a bit of research is always useful. Ideally, this involves working out what you might want to buy – and checking prices – before sales begin.

Once the sales are under way, comparing prices, delivery costs and delivery times at different stores can feel onerous and time-consuming, especially if you’re worried you might miss out on a deal.

To streamline their search for a bargain, some shoppers are turning to artificial intelligence (AI) tools to do the research for them.

Can AI really help you snag a deal? The answer is yes, maybe. But there are reasons to proceed carefully.

AI is being used to take the legwork out of all sorts of tasks. It makes sense consumers across the world are increasingly putting it to work as a shopping companion.

Say you’re looking for a new coffee machine or laptop this Black Friday. Rather than trawl through dozens of different sites yourself, you might ask a tool such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini to search the web for you and prepare a spreadsheet with a list of options.

title: Researchers map which gene versions brain cells use, cell by cell
content:
In complex organisms such as humans, the same gene can produce different RNA molecules. This is known as alternative splicing. The differently spliced RNA molecules, called isoforms, may in turn result in different proteins. 

Not all changes in isoforms have a visible effect. Sometimes, however, the wrong version can have drastic consequences. Incorrect isoforms have been associated with several brain diseases, including ALS, frontotemporal dementia and Alzheimer’s disease. 

“In these diseases, a protein named TDP-43 leaves its normal place in the cell and forms clumps, so it can no longer do its job," describes , University Researcher at the Department of Computer Science, University of Helsinki. 

"As a result, certain RNAs are spliced incorrectly, and neuronal cells lose proteins they need.” 

Detecting faulty splicing in the brain is not easy. Researchers at the University of Helsinki and  have now developed a method that maps which gene isoforms the cells in brain tissue use. In the future, it can also be used to identify faulty splicing. 

For this work, the team engineered new laboratory techniques as well as algorithms, software and statistical tools for analysing the data.

title: Nepal: Predatory Lending Abuses Exacerbated by Conflict in the Gulf
content:
(Tokyo) – Authorities in Nepal should hold illegal moneylenders accountable for abuses against borrowers, including unlawful land dispossession, arbitrary eviction, threats and acts of violence, and sexual exploitation, Human Rights Watch said today. Conflicts in the Gulf region, where many Nepalis are migrant workers facing exorbitant recruitment fees, have made more people vulnerable to extortion by illegal lenders.

“Despite government commitments to protect borrowers, illegal practices are rife in Nepal’s informal credit sector, leaving those with the fewest resources dependent on moneylenders who can take everything they own,” said Meenakshi Ganguly, Asia deputy director at Human Rights Watch. “The government of Prime Minister Balendra Shah should carry out the government’s commitments to ensure that the law against fraudulent and abusive lending is consistently enforced.”

Human Rights Watch interviewed 18 borrowers, as well as local government officials, lawyers, and activists from six districts in the Terai region where informal money lending is rampant, reviewed government reports, and examined over 50 cases in Nawalparasi district.

title: ‘Good intentions do not protect borders.’ New push for security boost in next EU budget
content:
More money for asylum and integration, tighter border controls and more effective returns, stronger internal security and greater solidarity among member states. These are the priorities shaping the European Parliament’s proposals for the EU’s next seven-year budget.

Three reports, three different priorities. And a bigger bill for the EU’s next multiannual financial framework (MFF). The European Parliament’s Civil Liberties Committe (LIBE) backed funding proposals covering migration, asylum and security policies.

But the proposals highlight the differing political priorities at play: while some lawmakers focus on tightening controls and returns, others insist that European migration policy must not be reduced merely to the defense of borders.

Lawmakers want to increase the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund to €13.31 billion. The European Commission had initially proposed €11.97 billion. The proposal also set aside two 15-per-cent shares of each member state’s allocation. One would go to the Common European Asylum System, including its external dimension. The other would support legal migration, integration, and social inclusion.

title: Indonesia: One year after devastating Aceh floods, communities face renewed flood risk as recovery stalls
content:
One year after catastrophic floods and landslides devastated Indonesia’s Aceh province, many survivors remain without adequate housing, continue to struggle to access promised support and now face renewed flood risks from this year’s rainy season, Amnesty International said in new research published today.

Amnesty’s briefing, A Continuing Crisis, found that many communities affected by the November 2025 disaster are still living with the consequences of inadequate response and recovery efforts. Many families remain in temporary shelters, damaged homes and makeshift accommodation, while reconstruction has progressed slowly and many survivors remain uncertain about what support they are entitled to receive.

“For the survivors in Aceh, this disaster did not end when the floodwaters receded. A year later, many families are still waiting for the housing and support they were promised by the Indonesian authorities,” said Montse Ferrer, Co-Regional Director at Amnesty International.

title: Serbian elections on Italian Wikipedia: from an editathon to a workshop
content:
The significance of the 2026 parliamentary elections in Serbia has extended beyond the borders of this Balkan country, becoming a topic of debate throughout Europe and beyond. Often, however, this has taken place without the minimum foundations required to do so productively.

To quote Luigi Einaudi, the second President of the Italian Republic, one must ‘first understand, then discuss, then decide’. Wikipedia still plays a vital role today in providing accurate political information, offering a source that aims for the greatest possible neutrality, rejecting both the political partisanship of many media outlets – often amplified by social media – and the complacent partisanship of artificial intelligence, where there is no fundamental truth but rather one that varies according to each user’s preferences.

Wikipedia, in fact, is the same for everyone, regardless of political orientation: there is no right-wing Wikipedia nor a left-wing Wikipedia; if someone has a problem with the facts and is unable to provide sources to back up their claims, that is their own problem!

title: Bringing Our Posts With Us: Internet Archive Europe Moves to Bonfire
content:
An archive should never lose its own history when it changes address.

Internet Archive Europe (IAE) is moving its fediverse home to Bonfire, an open source framework for federated social networks. You can now find us at @hq@community.internetarchive.eu. If you already follow us, you don’t need to do anything. Your follow moves with us.

The fediverse lets people talk to each other across thousands of independent servers that share the same open language. You can already leave one server for another and keep your name and your followers. On most fediverse software, though, your old posts stay behind on the server you left.

Bonfire’s migration tools change that. You can bring your post history with you, from another Bonfire server or from other fediverse software that exports an archive of your posts, and every post keeps its original date and link.

For an organisation whose mission is to preserve the web, this detail matters. We spend our days making sure the record survives when websites move, change or disappear. Our own record should survive our moves too.
snippet: An archive should never lose its own history when it changes address.

title: Senior Opposition Members Accuse Trump Administration of Failing to Pursue Elites Fueling Haiti Insecurity
content:
A letter by two senior United States lawmakers this week accused President Donald Trump’s administration of failing legal obligations to pursue the elites allegedly causing the gang violence that has plunged Haiti into a humanitarian crisis.

“By failing to name and sanction the political and economic elite fueling Haiti’s insecurity, the Administration allows those responsible to evade accountability and signals that their actions carry no consequences,” said the November 23 letter from New Hampshire Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen and New York Democratic Representative Gregory Meeks.

The Caribbean country has been in crisis since Haitian President Jovenel Moïse was assassinated in July 2021, in a plot for which five Haitian and American men so far have been convicted in U.S. federal court.

To fight armed criminal groups that have taken over swaths of the country, the United Nations last year deployed a Gang Suppression Force of roughly 2,000 personnel. This year, however, a record 1.5 million Haitians were displaced by violence, with more than half the 12 million population facing acute food insecurity.

title: NATO Needs Joint Solution to Critical Minerals Threat
content:
This is part of a series examining the central importance of critical minerals and the race to ensure Western supply.

Multiple US government agencies released a series of funding vehicles and new policies in August as part of efforts to build a reliable, non-Chinese, critical minerals supply chain for defense production. The announcements received relatively little fanfare outside the trade and business media, yet their ambitious goal is to reshape global supply chains.

China has spent decades developing an industrial ecosystem “from soup to nuts” controlled by the Communist Party. It built an integrated natural resource supply chain, financing system, production industry, trained labor force, and large domestic market as it pursued modernization and national security.

The US and Europe now see China’s dominance in critical minerals as a Western national security vulnerability. Without the minerals and rare earths China supplies, modern defense technology cannot be made at scale in the near term.

title: As window of opportunity closes on MFF budget negotiations: everything is still to play for
content:
On October 10, 2026, the disquieting news broke that the Irish Presidency of the Council of the European Union proposed cutting almost a third of future EU financial support for culture, media and civil society. This decrease was confirmed on November 21 by António Costa, President of the European Council.

It marked the latest twist in the protracted, complex negotiations over the EU’s long-term budget, the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), and specifically AgoraEU, the new flagship programme for democracy, civil society, media and culture.

Starting in January 2028, the MFF will total almost €2 trillion spending over the following seven years. Under the Irish Presidency’s proposal, AgoraEU’s budget would drop from €8.6 billion to about €6 billion.

This represents a saving of only around 0.2% of the total budget – yet it would profoundly impact Europe’s ability to fight disinformation, and to protect democracy, independent media and culture, according to those at the forefront of this work.

title: The Power of the Plenum: Leaderless Student Organising in Serbian and Croatian Student Movements
content:
Explore how leaderless, direct-democratic plenums have worked across student movements from Serbia’s 2026 student blockades to Croatia’s 2009 free-education occupation.

Plenums are open, non-hierarchical discussion and decision-making assemblies where every participant holds an equal voice, enabling movements to make decisions collectively without permanent leaders.

Plenums were used by students in Serbia in 2026, building on precedents such as the 2009 protests in Croatia, when students at the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences in Zagreb staged a monthlong occupation. Below is a collection of guides and articles about this decision making model.

If you have practical guides, reflections, or case studies on plenums to suggest please contact us.

title: Commission proposes Quantum Act and new Sovereign Tech Equity Fund to strengthen Europe's industrial capacity and security
content:
The European Commission today proposed the Quantum Act, a new framework to help turn Europe's quantum research into products and services, strengthen supply chains and prepare Europe's digital systems for post-quantum cryptography.

The proposal also lays the groundwork for the Sovereign Tech Equity Fund (STEF).

The impact of quantum technologies will be profound, from navigation without satellites and faster drug discovery to ultra-advanced batteries and next-generation secure communications. Quantum technologies are moving from laboratories to products and services.

The Quantum Act has three main pillars: research excellence, bringing quantum technology into use, and keeping systems and supplies secure. These will be delivered through the Quantum Europe Framework Initiative, which will bring together EU and national programmes around shared priorities for research and industry.

Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, said:

title: Fact check: How NATO was blamed for the vandalism of a Jesus statue in Vilnius
content:
Last week, reports emerged that a gold-coloured statue of Jesus had been removed from a wooden cross mounted on the courtyard wall of the Church of Divine Mercy, carried out into the street and smashed.

A video circulating on social media shows a man carrying the statue after removing it from the cross, while another man films the incident and laughs. The statue eventually falls onto the paving stones and breaks. The men involved quickly left the scene.

Lithuanian media reported that the police were notified of the incident at 00.47 on the 12th of November. On the 14th of November, law enforcement officers managed to establish the identity of the suspected perpetrator.

The suspect is a British national born in 1989 who was visiting Lithuania temporarily. However, following the incident, a precautionary measure was imposed on him – his identity document was confiscated, meaning that he is currently unable to leave Lithuania.

A pre-trial investigation has been launched into the desecration of a grave or another public memorial site.

title: Battle of Kyiv: Decoding tomorrow’s summit Ukraine showdown
content:
One of the Union’s defining dramas is to unfold tomorrow and Friday. Europe’s Ukraine loan faces a stern Brussels test. What are the odds?

The story has all the hallmarks of a historic clash of titans, minnows, and everybody in between. European Council President António Costa has put Ukraine’s financing on the agenda for the special summit on Thursday and Friday. Leaders will also discuss the 2028–2034 Multiannual Financial Framework, the EU’s long-term budget.

In Wednesday’s plenary debate, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen introduced the Ukraine package. She said: “We call it the Instrument for Coordinated Support for Ukraine. (Thus) Europe is covering two thirds of Ukraine’s financing need.”

The centrepiece is a Commission proposal for up to €45bn in additional support for Ukraine in 2027. Reports describe roughly €20bn for budget support and €25bn for military needs. The package would cover about two thirds of Ukraine’s estimated €70bn financing gap.

Who bears the borrowing costs is unsettled. Reporting says future interest payments remain unresolved and may affect the Ukraine allocation in the next budget.

title: Pull here to slow the climate crisis
content: Methane is a greenhouse gas responsible for roughly a third of today’s global heating, and it may be our best chance to curb the climate crisis. Compared to its better-known sibling carbon dioxide (CO₂), which can stay in the atmosphere for hundreds to thousands of years, methane's lifespan is relatively short at only about 12 years. That gives us a solid chance to slow down the climate crisis, according to the European Civil Society Observatory on Methane (CSO-M), and buy time to deal with CO₂ emissions. But where do we start if we want to hit the methane brake? If you imagine the EU's total methane emissions as a pie of three ingredients, one really is burping cows: the majority still come from agriculture. The second ingredient is organic waste, which releases methane as it breaks down in landfills. The third is fossil fuels. Methane can escape to the air in almost any stage of their life cycle, whether released intentionally or leaked by accident. Methane from the energy sector is also the easiest and most cost-effective to reduce, Maria Olczak, senior research fellow at the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, told The European Correspondent. content:
How can cooperation between countries lead to policy change, and how can that contribution be demonstrated? Coordinators from the EU strategies for the Baltic Sea, Danube and Alpine regions met in Stockholm on 12 November 2026. They compared how they implement action plans, engage stakeholders and assess results.

Anders Bergström and Asli Tepecik Dis of Föreningen Norden (Norden Association Sweden) hosted the meeting. Both serve as Policy Area Coordinators for Policy Area Education under the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR). The exchange focused on how macro-regional strategies contribute beyond individual projects. They bring together public authorities, practitioners and other partners to exchange knowledge and develop joint approaches. This helps connect their work to shared policy priorities.

title: FDA to Expand Prescription Drug Testing After ProPublica Revealed Safety Concerns
content:
The Food and Drug Administration will test more prescription drugs for impurities and other dangerous quality lapses under an expanded program described by safety experts as a critical step to better protecting America’s drug supply.

About 90% of prescriptions in the United States are for generic drugs, many manufactured thousands of miles away in countries that include India and China. Until now, the FDA has only periodically tested a sampling of those drugs to see if they were safe or worked as effectively as the brand-name medications they are meant to replicate.

Last week, the FDA announced it will test more often and identify poorly performing drugs for further study.

title: Raportti: Lapset saavat vain pienen siivun Suomen kehitysyhteistyörahoituksesta
content:
Suomen kehitysyhteistyörahoituksesta noin viidesosa osoitetaan lapsille. Osuus on viime vuosina kasvanut, mutta se johtuu osin kehitysyhteistyöleikkauksista, kertoo lastenjärjestö Suomen UNICEF tuoreen analyysinsä pohjalta.

Järjestö tutki Suomen kehitysyhteistyörahoitusta vuosina 2014–2024. Sinä aikana paljon on muuttunut: kehitysyhteistyörahoitus nousi huipputasoonsa vuonna 2022 mutta on sen jälkeen laskenut.

Lasten saaman rahoituksen osuus on näinä vuosina kyllä kasvanut muutaman prosenttiyksikön verran. Toisaalta leikkausten vuoksi euromääräinen kasvu on ollut vain 36 miljoonaa euroa, Unicef kertoo.

Yhteensä Suomi antoi vuonna 2024 noin 313 miljoonaa euroa lapsiin kohdistuvaa kehitysyhteistyörahoitusta.

Suomi saa Unicefilta kiitosta erityisesti terveys- ja koulutussektorien rahoituksesta, sillä siitä valtaosa kanavoidaan lapsille. Kumpikin on viime vuosina kuitenkin vähentynyt, lasten koulutusrahoitus peräti 57 prosenttia.

Humanitaarisesta avusta eli kriisien ja katastrofien yhteydessä annettavasta avusta vain 14 prosenttia menee lapsille.

title: Girlhood Studies: Secret Childhood Games on TikTok
content:
One secret childhood game that was never discussed with anyone. A secret played out with a friend, a sibling or a cousin, hidden from adults and later left unmentioned even between the players themselves.  Since around 2021, Russian-speaking TikTok has become an unexpected space where these memories surface. Short, humorous videos about “playing sex” pushed thousands of women to describe, in the comments, what they played, with whom and what happened afterwards. What emerges is a body of anonymous testimony about girlhood, play and sexuality.

It is difficult to establish when these games took place. Many commenters describe them in retrospect, but rarely say when they happened or how old they were at the time. As accounts are often private or anonymous, it is also difficult to determine the commenters’ own ages, and only a few state them explicitly. Some of those who do mention their age at the time say they were between 6 and 9. Some comments are written by young girls whose profile pictures or videos suggest, in my estimation, that they are around 13 to 15 years old.

title: Sverige och Ukraina fördjupar kultursamarbetet
content:
Samarbetet ska skapa nya möjligheter för kulturinstitutioner, akademiker, kulturutövare och studenter i båda länderna. 

Sverige är ett av de länder som prioriteras i Ukrainian Institutes strategi för 2026–2030. Samarbetet kommer att omfatta bland annat kulturutbyten, litteraturöversättning, teatersamarbeten och samverkan mellan universitet. 

– Ukrainas framtid formas inte bara genom EU-närmande och fysisk återuppbyggnad, utan också genom internationella samarbeten inom kultur, utbildning och forskning. Där ser vi nu till att Sverige blir en långsiktig partner, säger Madeleine Sjöstedt, generaldirektör för Svenska institutet. 

En övergripande målsättning för överenskommelsen är att skapa fler möjligheter för svenska och ukrainska kulturinstitutioner och universitet att utveckla långsiktiga gemensamma samarbeten.  

För Ukraina innebär samarbetet med Svenska institutet ökade möjligheter att delta i europeiska kultur- och kunskapssamarbeten och att bygga internationella nätverk för framtiden. För Sverige skapar det fördjupad kunskap om Ukraina och stärker relationerna med ett land som spelar en allt viktigare roll för Europas utveckling framöver.

title: Recent sinking of Russian vessels abroad shows the Russia-Ukraine war has officially gone global
content:
Ukraine has been executing a series of successful strikes against Russian assets around the world. Ukrainian forces disabled a Russian cargo vessel off the coast of Finland, and sunk a Russian corvette, the Merkury, along with damaging another cargo vessel, in Libyan waters.

These attacks, in the aftermath of Ukraine’s severe damage to the Kerch Strait Bridge in Russian-occupied Crimea, have created hope among Ukraine’s allies.

The year 2026 hasn’t advanced Ukraine’s goal of ending the war. A stagnant battlefront, increased Russian aerial attacks and a recalcitrant American president have increased the burdens on Ukraine’s government and its people.

Russia hasn’t had a good year either. More than 400,000 Russians have been killed in the war — and potentially as many as 700,000.

For Ukraine to have any chance of winning, it must increase the pressure on Russian leader Vladimir Putin’s government. Making Russian assets vulnerable globally is one way to do it.

Since its outset, the Russia-Ukraine conflict has had an international dimension. Ukraine’s allies, both prior to and after Russia’s full-fledged invasion in 2022, rushed supplies to Ukraine in its moment of need.

title: 50 years of the Sex Pistols: not agents of chaos, but dreamers of a utopia
content:
On November 26 1976, a London-based punk band released a record that created shock waves around the world.

While not the first punk single to be released (The Damned’s New Rose, Radio Birdman’s Burn my Eye EP, and I’m Stranded by the Saints were released a few weeks earlier), Anarchy in the UK, by the Sex Pistols set the tone and a high bar for what was to follow.

With its snarling lyrics (“I am an antichrist”) and raw sound, the song blew a gaping hole in 1970s complacency.

The Sex Pistols are often thought to be obnoxious anarchists who promoted chaos. But in many ways they were the opposite.

Here are five ways they created a template for a more inclusive, more tolerant, and better balanced society that remains relevant in today’s uncertain world.

Like many parts of the developed world, Britain in the mid-1970s faced economic decline, industrial unrest and growing disillusionment with established institutions.

Anarchy in the UK, followed by the band’s next single, God Save the Queen, released during Queen Elizabeth II’s Silver Jubilee in 1977, voiced the anger and alienation of many people while raising questions about national authority and identity.

title: Pieni Montenegro on testi EU:n laajentumiskyvylle
content:
EU valmistautuu laajenemaan, ja pisimmälle päässeen ehdokasmaan Montenegron jäsenyysneuvottelut lähestyvät loppusuoraa. Pienikokoinen Balkanin valtio olisi ehdokasmaista kenties helpoin integroida unioniin, mutta prosessi on tuonut esiin monia ongelmia aina uudistusten vauhdista naapurimaan vaatimuksiin ja siihen, miten varmistaa sujuva päätöksenteko entistä laajemmassa unionissa.

Euroopan unionin ehdokasmaiden kärjessä on 620 000 asukkaan Montenegro, joka pyrkii liittymään unionin 28. jäsenmaaksi vuoteen 2028 mennessä. Maan väestöstä 68 % kannattaa EU-jäsenyyttä, ja hallitus vie EU:n vaatimia uudistuksia eteenpäin kovaa vauhtia. 

Marraskuun alussa julkaisemassaan vuotuisessa laajentumispaketissa Euroopan komissio arvioi EU:n ehdokasmaiden tilannetta ja etenemistä jäsenyyspolulla. Komission mukaan Montenegro on suurimmaksi osin toteuttanut jäsenyysneuvotteluissa vaaditut uudistukset, ja neuvottelut voitaisiin saattaa päätökseen jo kuluvan vuoden loppuun mennessä. Tämän jälkeen Montenegron EU-jäsenyys vaatii vielä kaikkien nykyisten jäsenmaiden hyväksynnän.

title: Työväenmuseo Werstaalla kävi jo miljoonas vierailija
content:
Työväenmuseo Werstas ohitti tänään miljoonan kävijän rajan. Kävijälaskuri käynnistettiin museon muuttaessa nykyisiin tiloihinsa syksyllä 2001. Tamperelaismuseo on kasvattanut suosiotaan tasaisesti.

Museo kertoo tiedotteessa, että alussa kävijämäärä oli vaatimattomampi. Ensimmäinen vetonaula oli keväällä 2002 avattu Höyrykonemuseo, Suomen suurin tehdashöyrykone alkuperäisellä paikallaan. Seuraava kävijänousu koettiin, kun museo luopui pääsymaksuista 2010-luvun alussa.

Museonjohtaja Kalle Kallio arvioi, että maksuttomuuden lisäksi ihmisiä museoon vetää onnistuneet näyttelyvalinnat sekä toiminta tapahtumatalona.

– Werstaan ei-kaupallisesta kaupunkitilasta nauttivat niin tamperelaiset kuin matkailijatkin. Pääsymaksuttomuus mahdollistaa museokokemukset myös vähävaraisille perheille, opiskelijoille, työttömille eli aivan kaikenlaisille tamperelaisille. Olen erityisen iloinen lomaviikkojen vilinästä museon leikkipaikoilla, Kallio sanoo tiedotteessa.

Werstaan miljoonas vierailija oli Anne Huotari, joka yllätettiin kukkakimpulla, kun hän astui sisään museoon puoliltapäivin.

title: The Birds Are Listening: Scientists Used Seabirds to Track Hidden Ships
content:
In what sounds like an avian riff on The Wire, scientists equipped seabirds with audio recorders in order to listen in on their interactions with fishing vessels across the world’s oceans, according to a study published on Wednesday in Science Advances.

The approach exposed a large number of so-called “unseen” vessels that did not have their location trackers switched on. Many vessels are required to continuously signal their location using the Automatic Identification System (AIS), which openly broadcasts a ship’s location, similar to flight tracking. But AIS can be disabled for legitimate reasons—such as evading pirates—or with more nefarious motivations, such as concealment of illegal fishing activities. 

The new study was not designed to interrogate why any particular vessel switched off its AIS tracker. However, the discovery that seabirds are regularly interacting with unseen ships can shed light on broader efforts to monitor commercial fisheries, while also revealing new insights about seabird behavior, especially their risk of becoming “bycatch” when they are fatally trapped in fishing gear.

title: “I have never gotten used to the news”: Duaa Dhainy’s campaigning to halt Saudi Arabia’s executions and save lives
content:
More than 10 years ago, I began working with the European Saudi Organization for Human Rights, an organization founded by activists living in exile. Some had only recently fled Saudi Arabia to build new lives abroad, free from the fear of arrest and torture. Yet what they left behind continued to haunt them: friends in prison, families waiting for their children to be released, and fears for those still there. I would listen to my director, Ali al-Dubaisi, speaking about events in Saudi Arabia. Only later did I learn about the difficult journey he and his family had made into exile. I could see the responsibility he felt towards those who remained in Saudi Arabia, and how he turned it into daily work documenting violations and ensuring their voices were heard.

Over time, I realized that what I had first heard was only a fraction of what we would discover.

title: "Huna": Egyptian Author Abdelrahman ElGendy on Prison, National Book Award & Being Denied U.S. Visa
content:
This year’s annual National Book Awards ceremony in New York City was marked by the notable absence of nonfiction winner Abdelrahman ElGendy, after the Trump administration denied the Egyptian author entry into the United States. ElGendy’s debut, Huna: A Memoir of Revolution, Prison, and Becoming, chronicles his arrest and over six years of imprisonment, alongside his father, following arrest at a protest against the military dictatorship of Egypt’s President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi. After his release from prison in Egypt, ElGendy obtained an MFA in the United States but was forced to flee once again — this time from the U.S. to Europe — for fear of being targeted by immigration authorities over his criticism of Israel’s war on Gaza and U.S.-Egypt relations.

“It was a gutting thing to not be able to attend the ceremony. But it was also unsurprising,” ElGendy tells Democracy Now! about being barred from receiving the National Book Award in person. “[I] have labored for so long my whole life to get to this point, only to again and again and again be forced to witness it all from afar and detached from the people I love.”

title: MusicSphere at EuroXR 2026
content:
MusicSphere held its 4th General Meeting at the 23rd EuroXR International Conference (3rd-6th November) and participated in two sessions on the Cultural Heritage Cloud (ECCCH).

The MusicSphere Consortium at EuroXR 2026

The General Meeting on the 2nd-3rd November was held prior to the conference and brought together consortium partners to review the project’s progress, exchange updates on ongoing activities and plan the work for the next period by the different work packages.

Following this, MusicSphere participated in two sessions at EuroXR. The first of these was a 60 pitch minute session where a selection of ECCCH projects were presented by MusicSphere and EXCALIBUR, UNICHE and MNEME. This was followed on how the four initiatives could contribute to the wider European cultural heritage ecosystem, and the session concluded with a Q&A.

The second session was the ECCCH Technical Workshop: Exploring Integration and Interoperability which explored how the four projects could contribute to the ECCCH from a technical and practical perspective, focusing on interoperability, integration and the reuse of project results.

Read the full report on the MusicSphere website.

title: Amnesty: Gazan syntyvyys laskussa – tutkittava osana Israelin toteuttamaa kansanmurhaa
content:
Amnestyn uusi raportti No Conditions for Life: Women, Girls and the Gendered Dimensions of Israel’s Genocide Against Palestinians in Gaza (liitteenä) tarkastelee Israelin Gazassa toteuttaman kansanmurhan vaikutuksia erityisesti naisiin ja tyttöihin. Israel on vuosina 2023–2026 järjestelmällisesti tappanut, haavoittanut, pakkosiirtänyt ja nälkiinnyttänyt palestiinalaisia naisia ja tyttöjä sekä estänyt heitä saamasta välttämätöntä terveydenhuoltoa. Tämän seurauksena naisten mahdollisuudet tehdä omaa lisääntymisterveyttään, raskautta ja synnytystä koskevia päätöksiä eivät toteudu.

"Amnesty totesi yksiselitteisesti jo kaksi vuotta sitten, että Israel syyllistyy kansanmurhaan Gazassa. Uusi raportti osoittaa, miten syvällisesti kansanmurha on vaikuttanut juuri naisiin ja tyttöihin", sanoo Amnesty Internationalin pääsihteeri Agnès Callamard.

Gazan terveysministeriön mukaan Israel tappoi hyökkäyksillään 7.10.2023–1.10.2026 välillä yhteensä 22 331 naista ja tyttöä. He muodostavat noin 30 prosenttia kaikista kuolonuhreista. Kansanmurhan kahden ensimmäisen vuoden aikana Israel tappoi keskimäärin 30 naista tai tyttöä joka päivä.

title: Latest updates on the HiLIFE tenure track call
content:
The most recent HiLIFE tenure track call for assistant/associate professors has closed on November 16, 2026. We were thrilled to receive a record-breaking total of 745 applications. 

A significant number of applications were sent in from the following locations: Finland (192), the United States (103), Germany (70), and Sweden (47). The same countries were also topping our statistics in the previous Tenure Track calls. Based on the applicants’ responses, the most represented primary ERC LS panels were LS8, LS1, and LS5.

The Appointment Committee will soon begin the first-stage evaluation; the applicants can expect to receive the results by mid-March 2027.

Following the initial evaluation, the shortlisted candidates will go through a 2nd stage external evaluation during March - April 2027. Selected applicants are then invited to interviews held in late May – early June 2027. 

The entire recruitment process is due to be finalized in September 2027, with the announcement of new HiLIFE tenure track assistant and associate professors.

If you have any questions about the recruitment, please contact hilife-recruit(at)helsinki.fi.

title: Hong Kong: Fire Anniversary Underscores Growing Repression
content:
(London) – The Hong Kong government should ensure meaningful accountability for the devastating fire that killed 168 people one year ago and end its suppression of peaceful criticism, Human Rights Watch said today.

On November 26, 2025, Hong Kong’s deadliest fire in decades engulfed seven residential high-rise buildings at Wang Fuk Court, Tai Po. The authorities initiated an independent investigation and arrested three dozen people implicated in crimes. The Housing Minister resigned. But the authorities have also threatened and arbitrarily arrested those engaging in criticism and activism concerning the fire.

“The Hong Kong government responded to the horrific Wang Fuk Court fire by using Beijing’s tactics of shutting out the voices of the victims and promising an elusive accountability,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The authorities need to recognize that the only way to prevent similar tragedies in the future is to allow people to speak out safely and hold those responsible fully accountable.”

The authorities have engaged in apparent acts of repression of free expression in the weeks ahead of the anniversary:
