title: Tutustu uuteen maksuttomaan materiaaliin merkityksellisestä kestävästä elämästä
content:
Viime viikolla julkistettiin Elämänjalotus, maksuton koulutusmateriaali merkityksellisestä kestävästä elämästä. Materiaalin pohjalta voi pohdiskella omia elämän valintojaan, ottaa kestävän elämäntavan puheeksi erilaisissa ryhmissä tai vaikka järjestää työpajoja ja keskustelutilaisuuksia yhdistyksissä.

Materiaalin on tuottanut Kestävää elämäntapaa edistävä siirtymäliike Jalotus ry yhdessä tutkijoiden Tuuli Hirvilammen (Tampereen yliopisto), Frank Martelan (Aalto-yliopisto) ja Annukka Vainion (Helsingin yliopisto) kanssa. Kehitystyön on rahoittanut Maj ja Tor Nesslingin säätiö. Sisältö perustuu siis tutkittuun tietoon, eikä sen käyttäminen vaadi kestävyysasiantuntijuutta. Kotiseutuliitto oli mukana kehitystyössä kokeilu- ja kommentointikumppanina.

Materiaali tarkastelee merkityksellistä kestävää elämää kolmella muutoksen kehällä: maailmankuvallinen, yhteiskunnallinen ja käytännöllinen muutos. Jokaisella kehällä on asiantuntijavideoita, keskustelutehtäviä sekä konkreettisia tekoja, joihin voi tarttua yksin. Lisäksi koulutusmateriaalista saa kasan lukusuosituksia, joiden avulla voi perehtyä aiheisiin syvällisemmin.

title: EU rejects Trump’s case for new tariffs
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission on Wednesday rejected Washington’s claim that Europe is fueling global industrial overcapacity, after the Trump administration proposed a 15% tariff on the 27-country bloc.

“We will study the findings. At the same time we strongly reject the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity. To the contrary, Europe is among those most exposed to overcapacity,” Olof Gill, the Commission’s deputy chief spokesperson, said in a statement. 

“The EU and the U.S. share a real concern about global overcapacity, much of it state-driven and concentrated in third countries. We regret the lack of joint action,” he added. 

The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, led by Jamieson Greer, found that 14 trading partners, including the European Union, China and Japan, had artificially deflated prices by flooding markets with manufactured goods. The decision follows a trade investigation launched in March.

Greer on Wednesday proposed a 15% tariff on the European Union, in line with the ceiling agreed in the transatlantic trade truce struck in July 2025 between U.S. President Donald Trump and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

title: Suhdannekysely: Arkkitehtialan palkansaajien lomautukset vähenivät – yrityksissä tilanne kahtiajakautunut
content:
Suomen Arkkitehtiliiton (SAFA), Arkkitehtitoimistojen liiton (ATL) ja Suomen maisema-arkkitehtiliiton (MARK) lokakuussa toteutettuun suhdannekyselyyn vastasi 261 henkilöä, joista 59 oli yrittäjiä ja loput palkansaajia.

Yrittäjävastaajien raportoimat lomautukset olivat kesällä lähes puolittuneet vuoden 2024 huipusta, mutta nyt ne ovat kääntyneet uudelleen nousuun. Lomautuksista ilmoitti 34 prosenttia vastanneista yrittäjistä (kesällä 24 %). Irtisanomisia oli toteuttanut 16 prosenttia yrittäjistä, ja 22 prosentilla lomautukset ovat suunnitteilla.

Hankkeiden peruuntuminen on edelleen yleistä. Kesällä vajaa kolmannes yrittäjistä kertoi peruuntuneista hankkeista, nyt osuus oli 38 prosenttia. Hankkeiden viivästyksistä raportoi 64 prosenttia yrittäjistä.

Palkansaajista 29 prosenttia raportoi oman työpaikkansa henkilöstön lomautuksista edeltävän puolen vuoden aikana, kun kesällä osuus oli 39 prosenttia. Tilanne näyttää paremmalta myös viranomaistilastoissa, mutta kuva on silti epätäydellinen.

title: Äitiyden myyttiä purkamassa
content:
Pertti Rautiainen

Laura Juntunen ei kirjoissaan väistele vaikeita aiheita. Hänen esikoisteoksensa Subutex-kaupungin kasvatit käsitteli Raahen huumausainepiirejä, omaelämäkerrallinen Tyttö joka en taas syömishäiriötä, päihderiippuvuutta ja seksuaalista hyväksikäyttöä. Kodittomuuteen keskittyneen Koti kadulla -teoksen jälkeen hän tarttuu äitiyden moniin kasvoihin ja myytteihin tuoreimmassa teoksessaan Pyhät pahat äidit.

Kirjan rakenne on hieman erikoinen. Siinä seurataan kirjoittajan raskauden edistymistä, synnytystä ja ensimmäisiä vauvakuukausia, ja toisaalta Juntunen on haastatellut hyvin erilaisia ja eri elämäntilanteissa olevia äitejä. Hän on myös käyttänyt paljon tutkimuskirjallisuutta. Kirja on sekoitus autofiktiota, tietokirjaa ja lopulta myös pamflettia.

Yksi teoksen keskeisistä teemoista on se, että kuva äitiydestä on paljon todellisuutta suppeampi. Näin on yksittäisten ihmisten laita, samoin median, poliitikoista ja talouselämästä puhumattakaan. Vaikuttaa siltä, että äidin rooli halutaan joskus tietoisestikin määrittää varsin ahtaasti ja usein samalla ristiriitaisesti.

title: At the listening centre, women are able to speak freely
content:
WOMEN SIT IN LITTLE GROUPS in a small courtyard. One group is rolling soap paste into balls, whilst another is kneading dough by hand. A third group is working with sewing machines. We are at the ‘listening centre’ run by Finn Church Aid (FCA) for women: a place where women can come when they are facing problems.

Everyday life in Paoua is challenging. The region has a turbulent recent history, and the scars of the most recent conflict, which was at its worst in 2013–2014, are still visible both in the ruined buildings and in people’s behaviour. Violence flares up quickly, and this is evident in people’s homes too.

“I came here for the first time because my husband was abusing me,” says Dendo Rosine, one of the women who’s making soap.

She is still missing several front teeth.

“I received help from the listening centre. I was given emotional support and help with keeping in touch with the hospital. The centre’s staff also spoke to my husband. Things are calmer at home now,” Dendo Rosine continues.

Her story is very common amongst the women who come to the centre.

title: Event Blog | After the US Midterms: What the Results Mean for America and the World
content:
On 10 November, the Foreign Policy Centre (FPC) and Leiden University brought together policymakers, academics, practitioners, students, and members of civil society in a packed Committee Room at the Palace of Westminster to examine what the 2026 US midterm election results mean for the United States and its partners around the world.

Chaired by Lord Robertson of Port Ellen, the event brought together Dr Andrew Gawthorpe, Associate Professor at Leiden University and Senior Research Fellow at FPC; Kevin Maloney, Chief Public Affairs Officer at Carnegie Council for Ethics in International Affairs; Laurel Rapp, Director of the US and North America Programme at Chatham House; and Professor Mel Bunce, Professor of International Journalism and Politics at City St George’s, University of London.

The event focused on three broad questions: what the midterms revealed about US politics; how the new balance of power could affect US foreign policy; and what developments the UK, Europe and other partners should now be watching.

title: ATO 2026: Sharing is caring – Open data for Open Source compliance
content:
In October, the OSI hosted the State of the Source track at All Things Open designed to connect developers with the big policy conversations shaping our ecosystem. Nick Vidal and Brian Duran, members of the ClearlyDefined Outreach Committee, presented “Sharing is caring: Open data for Open Source compliance.”

Open Source compliance depends on accurate data about millions of software components, yet organizations often duplicate efforts and build isolated datasets. ClearlyDefined offers a better approach: shared, community-verified open data on software component provenance, license, and vulnerabilities that improves accuracy, reduces duplication, and enables compliance automation at scale.

Nick Vidal: Hello. Good morning, everyone. We’re going to be continuing the conversation. McCoy gave a great presentation around open source licensing, and now we’re going to be getting into compliance. We want to present a really interesting project called ClearlyDefined. The idea behind ClearlyDefined is sharing license data. Let’s first start with who we are.

My name is Nick Vidal. I work with the OSI. I’m a community manager, and this is my colleague Brian.

title: Varuskuntien kirjastot ovat vapaaehtoisten varassa
content:
Lukeminen ei enää varusmiespalvelustaan suorittavia innosta. Tästä saatiin käytännön osoitus tänä syksynä.

Aiemmin Kirkkonummen kirjastoauto Ella pysähtyi Upinniemen varuskunnan lähistöllä, mutta tänä syksynä pysäkki poistettiin käytöstä.

Kirkkonummella sijaitseva Upinniemen varuskunta on Suomen suurin merivoimien tukikohta, jossa koulutetaan parituhatta asevelvollista vuosittain. Potentiaalisia asiakkaita olisi siis vaikka kuinka paljon.

”Upinniemen alueella olleet kirjastoauton pysäkit ovat vuosien varrella vähentyneet, koska asiakkaita ei enää ollut. Aikoinaan oli pari pysäkkiä varuskunta-alueen sisällä, mutta varusmiehiä ei asioinut kirjastoautossa”, kertoo Kirkkonummen pääkirjasto Fyyrin palveluvastaava Jaana Heimo.

Onko kirjasto harkinnut yhteydenpitoa varuskunnan kanssa?

”Kirjastoauton reittejä ja pysäkkien käyttöä seurataan aktiivisesti, pysäkkitoiveita pyydetään kuntalaisilta ja ne huomioidaan mahdollisuuksien mukaan”, Jaana Heimo kommentoi.

Upinniemessä toimivasta sotilaskodista kerrotaan, että myöskään siellä ei ole enää vuosiin ollut omaa kirjastoa.

Nyt lähin kirjastoautopysäkki on seitsemän kilometrin päässä, ja pääkirjasto Fyyri noin 14 kilometrin matkan päässä.

YK:ssa valmistellaan mittavia uudistuksia, joiden tavoitteena on tehdä järjestön toiminnasta entistä yhtenäisempää ja tuloksellisempaa. Kehityspoliittisen toimikunnan (KPT) keskustelupaperin mukaan uudistuksen onnistumista mitataan ennen kaikkea sillä, kuinka hyvin YK pystyy vastaamaan kehittyvien maiden tarpeisiin ja saamaan aikaan konkreettisia tuloksia.

YK:n pääsihteeri António Guterresin käynnistämällä YK80-uudistuksella pyritään vähentämään päällekkäisyyksiä ja vahvistamaan YK-järjestöjen yhteistyötä. Uudistuspaineita lisäävät konfliktit, ilmastokriisi ja luontokato sekä kehitysrahoituksen leikkaukset, jotka vaikeuttavat kasvaviin tarpeisiin vastaamista.

Suomella on mahdollisuus vaikuttaa uudistuksen suuntaan muun muassa YK:n päätöksentekoelimissä, rahoitusvalinnoilla ja kansainvälisellä yhteistyöllä, todetaan kehityspoliittisen toimikunnan keskustelupaperissa Uudistuva YK ja Suomen vaikuttamisen suunnat.

Keskustelupaperissa arvioidaan, että YK-järjestöjen yhteistyö on vahvistunut. Erilliset ohjaus- ja rahoitusjärjestelmät ylläpitävät kuitenkin päällekkäisyyksiä ja kilpailua voimavaroista.

title: Rauhankasvatusinstituutilla on uusi hallitus ja strategia
content:
Rauhankasvatusinstituutin syyskokouksessa valittiin hallitus vuodelle 2027 ja hyväksyttiin uusi strategia vuosille 2027–2031. Uusi strategia suuntaa rauhankasvatustyötä muuttuvassa maailmassa ja vahvistaa rauhankasvatuksen roolia yhteiskunnallisten haasteiden ratkaisemisessa ja kestävän rauhan rakentamisessa.

Rauhankasvatusinstituutin hallituksen puheenjohtajana jatkaa Saara Särmä ja varapuheenjohtajana Milla Ilonen.

Hallitukseen kaksivuotiskaudelle 2027–2028 valittiin Juulia Järvenpää, Tomi Kiilakoski, Elisa Sarpo ja Zahra Karimy sekä uusina jäseninä Camilla Ojala, Inka Kärki Nemeh ja Emmi Nuorgam. Hallituksessa jatkavat kaksivuotiskautensa toista vuotta Annina Laaksonen, Tytti Voutilainen ja Pia Lundbon.

Lämpimästi tervetuloa uusille hallituksen jäsenille ja suuri kiitos kautensa päättäville jäsenille yhteisestä työstä rauhankasvatuksen edistämiseksi!

Maailma muuttuu nopeasti. Monikriisien ajassa sodat, eriarvoisuus, demokratian murentuminen, rasismi, ilmastokriisi ja yhteiskuntien polarisaatio haastavat tapojamme elää yhdessä. Samalla ne haastavat myös rauhankasvatusta uudistumaan.

title: The Guardian view on the next UN secretary general: sacrificing principles will damn the institution, not save it | Editorial
content:
The UK must continue to oppose the UAE’s tainted nominee, Lana Nusseibeh. The ethical course is also the pragmatic one

The future of the United Nations has rarely looked more perilous in an age of impunity for atrocities, raging wars, open US hostility, a funding crisis and security council deadlock. It is widely agreed that the choice of its next secretary general is critical – perhaps even existential. Unfortunately, that’s where agreement ends.

Under the opaque selection system, security council members are privately polled on their views of each candidate. A “discourage” vote from one of the five permanent members is diplomacy-speak for a veto. Only when a consensus emerges does the general assembly get a say on the candidate. The next straw poll is due on Monday, with no deal yet in sight. With António Guterres completing his term on 31 December, the seat could fall empty for the first time.

title: Attiéké, Abodan and a Whole Lot of Open Knowledge: My WikiIndaba Reflections
content:
Some discoveries happen in conference rooms, others happen over a plate of food or during a cultural performance. At WikiIndaba, I had my fair share of all three.

Did you know that the traditional skills involved in making Attiéké are recognised by UNESCO as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity? And that the dance I initially thought was Adowa was actually Abodan? What an epiphany!

These were just two of the many things I discovered at WikiIndaba. Beyond the sessions, presentations and conversations, the conference offered an opportunity to learn about other cultures, reflect on the work we do as Wikimedians and, importantly, think about where our movement is headed.

As we celebrate 25 years of the Wikimedia movement, I left with several thoughts about knowledge equity, African languages, community development and how we can make the knowledge we create more visible and accessible.

Here are a few reflections that stayed with me.

title: Oil Smuggling Crackdown Sets Up Collision Between Baghdad and Kurdistan Region
content:
Iraq's prime minister has dismissed several senior officials over alleged oil smuggling in the autonomous Kurdistan region and ordered federal authorities to take control of oilfields and border crossings in northern areas. 

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi removed the head of the Border Ports Authority, suspended the director general of the state-owned North Oil Company and dismissed several senior security officials, while directing federal authorities to assume control of oilfields in Diyala, Kirkuk, Salahuddin and Nineveh provinces as well as border crossings in areas under Kurdish control, citing national sovereignty and the protection of national resources.

The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) has rejected the moves as unconstitutional. KRG Interior Minister Rebar Ahmed said the region will not abide by Baghdad's “unilateral decisions,” calling al-Zaidi's orders unconstitutional and contrary to “the spirit of federalism.”

Iraqi political analyst Lawk Ghafuri told OCCRP on Wednesday that “everyone is worried about what will happen. The situation for the people is tense.”

title: An Icelandic Home Guard to Help Secure the North Atlantic
content:
The sparsely populated and remote island was a founding member of NATO in 1949, and is unique amongst the alliance’s members as it has no military. It relies instead on a bilateral defense agreement with the US and serves the alliance by providing facilities for surveillance, transit, and monitoring operations.

But it cannot continue to depend on NATO assets to solve basic military tasks and provide surveillance forever, particularly from hostile powers which want to use its territory for hybrid and kinetic warfare. NATO is short of personnel and seeking more manpower to face the Russian threat. It’s time Iceland shouldered its weight.

The alliance’s anti-submarine and surveillance aircraft patrolling the Greenland-Iceland-UK gap, and the intelligence units that help to keep it safe need protection at their bases. Iceland also needs to safeguard transportation assets for routes between Europe and North America.

The island is not massive, but it is still a significant territory, more than double the size of Denmark and equal to the US state of Kentucky. Even if a part of its landmass is made up of glaciers and active volcanoes, it is still a considerable landmass.

title: The latest on Warsaw’s push for a permanent US military base in Poland
content:
There are currently around 10 000 US troops stationed in Poland. Most of them are deployed on a rotational basis, but Warsaw wants to ensure that some of this contingent remains in the country permanently. At present, only six European countries host permanent US military bases: Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom, Spain, Turkey, and Belgium.

Following talks in Washington with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, Poland’s defence minister said on Tuesday, the 10th of November, that his American counterpart had assured him that “everything is moving in the right direction”.

“In our understanding, this means that the Pentagon has given the green light to a permanent US military base in Poland,” Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said, although the project has yet to receive official US approval.

The Pentagon did not directly confirm that the military base would be established, nor did it confirm the previously reported December deadline for a decision. However, in its comments, it acknowledged that discussions were continuing on strengthening the US military presence in Poland.

title: Dear government, here's some money
content: If I could write a wishlist to the government, it’d be long. Dear government, free public transport for everyone, better education, and more support for cultural projects, please. They’d read it with a smile and a nod, then promptly tell me to give up. How are they supposed to pay for all that? State budgets across Europe are already under pressure. Luckily, I found a solution. Or at least the start of one. European banks are sitting on billions of euros in so-called dormant accounts. When people move abroad, or die without leaving any heirs or telling their heirs about their savings, their bank accounts are often forgotten and left untouched for decades. They become dormant assets – ghost money, if you will. In Germany, estimates for how much money is sitting in dormant accounts range from €4-9 billion. €9 billion! Currently, German banks pocket that money as their own income after 30 years, although if the owner somehow remembers their money later on, they can still claim it back. title: Democrats Vow to Shield Smithsonian From Any Trump Overhaul
content:
A top congressional Democrat announced she will investigate the Trump White House’s potential overhaul of the leadership and curatorial decisions at the Smithsonian Institution, the independent agency that oversees 21 national museums.

In a letter sent on Tuesday to the Smithsonian’s Board of Regents, Rep. Chellie Pingree, D-Maine, cited ProPublica’s recent story on the draft plans by a White House staffer targeting one of the Smithsonian’s most prominent museums, calling the reporting “extremely concerning.”

Pingree, who is slated to lead the subcommittee that controls the Smithsonian’s funding in the next Congress, said the plans revealed in the ProPublica story align with the administration’s broader efforts to interfere with the Smithsonian, which receives federal funding but is governed by a 17-person Board of Regents whose members include the chief justice of the United States, members of Congress, the vice president and private citizens.

title: Who is Pedro Sánchez – and what has eight years of ‘sanchismo’ meant for Spanish politics?
content:
Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez means many different things to many different people. On the Spanish right he offers a target, a figure around whom a range of grievances converge to rally and mobilise voters. On the left, he can inspire appreciation for what two terms of Spanish Socialist Party (PSOE) government have achieved, as well as fear of a right-wing rollback and anger over government failures.

Perceptions of Sánchez have changed massively since he took office in 2018, following a vote of no confidence against Mariano Rajoy’s conservative People’s Party (PP) government. After being re-elected by a whisker in 2023, his ability to garner support in Spain’s complex political landscape has become a hallmark of his leadership.

But the same negotiating skill that his supporters celebrate as proof of resilience and pragmatism reinforces, among his opponents, the image of a leader whose greatest priority is to cling on to power, whatever the cost.

The right often highlights “Sanchismo” as the root of all that is wrong in Spanish politics. But there is, in reality, no such ideology or movement. So what is sanchismo?

title: Jensen Huang’s controversial return to Nvidia poses the question – what’s the point of a board?
content:
It’s hard to think of Nvidia without picturing Jensen Huang. Rarely seen without his signature black leather jacket, Huang has led chipmaker Nvidia since co-founding it in 1993, turning it into a central player in the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.

Earlier this month, Huang resigned as president, chief executive officer and a member of Nvidia’s board, in the wake of a bombshell scandal involving affairs and alleged corporate espionage.

Days later, the board linked his departure to “personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards and cultural norms”. It said it did “not intend to reinstate” him.

This week, however, it voted unanimously to bring him back, following a remarkable intervention by US President Donald Trump.

Many analysts have already weighed in on why the US government intervened. But there’s a deeper, more fundamental question here about corporate power.

If a chief executive is seen as too valuable to lose, can a company’s board still hold them to account? If it can’t, what exactly is the board for?

title: “I wish they could pass the bill today”: Ghanaian women accused of being witches on long-awaited legislation
content:
In Ghana, people accused of witchcraft, primarily older women, face threats, physical attacks and in some cases, death. They have no safe place to escape to other than camps in Northern and North-eastern regions overseen by religious leaders, as documented in Amnesty International’s 2025 report.

In 2023, the Anti-Witchcraft Accusations Bill, which seeks to establish a legal framework for addressing accusations of witchcraft and related abuses, including the protection and reintegration of persons affected, was passed by parliament as a private members’ bill. However, it was not signed into law by the then president, who cited constitutional concerns.  

In July 2026, the bill was reintroduced to Ghana’s Parliament as a private members bill. Since September, the government is moving to take over the bill as a government-sponsored bill, aiming to facilitate its passage and implementation. The Minister of Gender confirmed that government was working towards reintegration of camp residents and eventual closure of the camps.

Amnesty International visited three of these camps, in Gambaga, Kukuo and Gnani, in April and May 2026, where six resident women shared their stories and hopes.

title: "Disaster Waiting to Happen": Iowa Declares Emergency as U.S. Army Detonates 5 Tons of Lead Azide
content: The U.S. Army detonated nearly five tons of highly unstable lead-based explosives at an ammunition plant in southeastern Iowa on Wednesday, potentially sending toxic lead dust and other deadly contaminants spewing across communities and farmland throughout the Mississippi River water basin. Residents, who were first informed last week, had been ordered to evacuate or else shelter in place. “The Army has decided to act as it wishes, and it is going against the recommendations of its own experts,” says Pat Elder, who tracks how military activity impacts people and the planet at the Military Poisons project. “There is no reason for this to be done, and it is a disaster waiting to happen.”

title: Väestöliiton Perhebarometri 2026: Suomalaiset toivovat yhteiskunnalta enemmän tukea perheille
content:
Väestöliiton Perhebarometri 2026 Kuka hoitaa? tarkastelee suomalaisten kokemuksia ja mielipiteitä siitä, miten yhteiskunta on onnistunut perheiden tukemisessa. Vain joka neljäs suomalainen arvioi, että valtiovalta tukee perheitä riittävästi. Enemmistö suomalaisista poistaisi monet pienituloisten lapsiperheiden tukiin tehdyt heikennykset. Nykyinen perhevapaajärjestelmä koetaan melko hyväksi, mutta silti lapset menevät kodin ulkopuoliseen hoitoon keskimäärin selvästi aiemmin kuin vanhemmat toivoisivat.

Perhebarometrit ovat jo vuodesta 2014 kysyneet kansalaisilta arvosanaa hallituksen perhepolitiikalle. Yleisarvosanat ovat nyt paikoin heikompia kuin aiempina vuosina. Vain neljännes arvioi, että perheitä tuetaan riittävästi. Enemmistö arvioi tuen olleen epäjohdonmukaista ja perheiden kahtiajaon voimistuneen.

Useampi kuin joka toinen suomalainen arvioi, ettei lapsiperheiden palveluihin panosteta nykyisellään riittävästi. Lapsiperheiden vanhempien mielestä nykyisistä palveluista parhaiten toimivat neuvolat. Toiseksi parhaiten arvioidaan toimivan järjestöjen ja seurakuntien palvelut. Huonoiten toimivat mielenterveyspalvelut ja tilapäinen kotipalvelu vanhempien kuormitustilanteessa.

title: 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence
content:
Every year during the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence women’s rights defenders come together to remember women facing violence—including those we have lost—and to renew the struggle for gender equality.

This year we face growing gender inequality, as the rights of women and girls are rolled back and threatened by authoritarianism and conflict in many countries. Across all regions, governments and powerful anti-rights movements seek to dismantle hard-won rights for women and girls. Technology is adding new dimensions to abuse, from online harassment and surveillance to digitally enabled threats, violence, and sexualized deepfake images;  women politicians are often targeted.

In the United States and Russia, authorities are dismantling reproductive rights. In Africa, lawmakers, with support from foreign conservative groups, are promoting a charter aiming to roll back women’s rights across the continent. In Argentina, funding for preventing GBV has been scrapped.

content:
The European Parliament voted by large majorities to send seven proposals for the EU’s next long-term budget straight into negotiations with the Council, heading off a possible challenge from the far right.

The lawmakers were voting on the proposals for Global Europe, the European Social Fund, Horizon Europe, the Connecting Europe Facility, the European Competitiveness Fund, the asylum and migration program and AgoraEU. 

These proposals are now moving to negotiations with the Council of the European Union based on reports adopted by the committees responsible for each file.

title: Pääkirjoitus: Varusmiehille sopisi lukutuokio
content:
Tänä syksynä uutisoitiin isoista muutoksista, joita on tehty varusmiesten koulutukseen. Maastossa ei nukuta aina enää puolijoukkueteltoissa kaminan loimussa, sillä tällainen majoitus on lämpökameralla varustetulle droonille helppo maalitaulu.

Sen sijaan varusmiehet nukkuvat Ylen jutun mukaan metsässä erillään toisistaan makuupussin, naamioverkon ja puuston suojissa.

Jutussa haastatellun koulutuspäällikön mukaan varusmiesten koulutus on muuttunut lyhyessä ajassa paljon. Varusmiehet ovat entistä vähemmän luokkahuoneissa.

”Olemme karsineet kaiken ylimääräisen pois. Nyt keskitytään nimenomaan taistelukoulutukseen ja taistelukentällä oloon.”

Pohdin kouluttajan sanoja tänä syksynä, kun selvittelin, millaisia kirjastopalveluja varusmiehille on tarjolla. Kävi ilmi, että niitä on tarjolla heikosti.

Kymmenessä varuskunnassa on Puolustusvoimien ylläpitämä kirjasto, mutta ne eivät tarjoa varusmiehille vapaa-ajan lukemista. Tätä palvelua hoitavat sotilaskodit, mutta niiden ylläpitämien kirjastojen resurssit ovat pienet. Ne pyörivät täysin vapaaehtoisten voimin eivätkä esimerkiksi saa valtiolta avustusta. Lue juttumme aiheesta painetusta Kirjastolehdestä.

title: Turkmen Wikipedia: The Quiet, Resilient Corner of the Free Encyclopedia
content:
Every language edition of Wikipedia has its own heartbeat. Some move at breakneck speed, shaped by thousands of daily contributors, sprawling WikiProjects, and automated bots. Others grow slowly, steadily, and quietly-held together by a small circle of dedicated volunteers who care deeply about seeing their language represented in the world’s largest free knowledge repository.

Turkmen Wikipedia (tk.wikipedia.org) belongs to that second group.

At first glance, a smaller Wikipedia can look understated compared to larger regional neighbors like Russian, Turkish, or Uzbek Wikipedias. Yet behind the modest article counts and quieter Recent Changes feed lies a remarkably resilient project-one where every well-sourced paragraph, every standardized template, and every newly created article carries outsized meaning for readers searching in Turkmen.

According to Meta-Wiki’s List of Wikipedias, Turkmen Wikipedia sits around 200th place among all active language editions-a compact, steadily maintained project with deep room to grow

title: The EU Could Soon be Tracking Irish Alumina Shipments to Russia Amid Defense-Industry Scrutiny
content:
The European Commission has proposed new reporting rules on alumina exports to Russia amid concerns that output from a Russian-owned refinery in Ireland is feeding Russia’s weapons industry.

“We can confirm that in the 22nd sanctions package we have proposed to include a reporting mechanism for all aluminium oxide trade with Russia,” European Commission spokesperson Siobhan McGarry told OCCRP. “This would include the Aughinish plant while not limited to it.”

The measure will allow the union “to establish a complete picture of alumina flows between the EU and Russia to confirm that it does not end up directly or indirectly being used in Russia’s military equipment,” McGarry added.

The proposal follows a March investigation by OCCRP and its partners — iStories, KibOrg, De Tijd, The Irish Times, The Guardian, and Delfi — that exposed links between the Irish refinery and Russian defense contractors.

Using shipping and trade records, reporters traced bauxite from Brazil and Guinea to Aughinish, where it is processed into alumina. The refinery, owned by Russian aluminum giant Rusal, then exports the material to its parent company’s smelters in Russia.

title: Murder Is Love, Says Putin Preacher
content:
Lest you were wondering just why Mother Russia is killing large numbers of Ukrainian civilians — including babies, toddlers, and children — every day, her favorite crackpot philosopher has the answer.

No, it’s not because, as Vladimir Putin likes to say, Ukrainians are neo-Nazis hellbent on joining NATO and lobbing nukes at Russia. Nor is it because Ukrainians have banned the Russian language and culture (which would come as a surprise to Ukraine’s Russian-speaking Ukrainians).  

Instead, says Aleksandr Dugin, Mother Russia’s influential answer to the Nazi philosopher Alfred Rosenberg, it’s all because of her great love for Ukrainians. According to Dugin’s November 7 interview, love is the culprit: “We love you, we respect you,” he says to Ukrainians, “and even if we have to kill you, we shoot our own brothers and sisters in the heart, in the face, in the head.”

title: UK and EU strike three key deals, but thorny issues remain
content:
A decade after the Brexit referendum, London and Brussels are seeking to rebuild a relationship that for years has been marked by disputes over borders, trade and regulation. Today’s (20 November) EU-UK summit delivered tangible results in several key areas.

Negotiations were concluded on three agreements covering opportunities for young people to work and study, measures to facilitate food trade, and the linking of emissions trading systems. Timetables for their implementation were also agreed. Before the new rules can come into force, however, the agreements still need to be formally concluded.

“It has been 10 years since Brexit, but I think today we can all say with confidence that this is a good day for Britain and a good day for Europe. The agreement we have reached together benefits both sides and meets the expectations of the British people,” the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, said after the summit.

However, disputes over student tuition fees and cooperation in the electricity market remain unresolved. London is also still seeking assurances that British companies will not lose out as a result of EU plans to support European industry.

title: Why is it getting so hard to watch football?
content: It's Champions League night. Nine matches are on the schedule. Millions of fans will tune in, some through paid streaming services, others via illegal websites. Either way, watching the beautiful game is getting increasingly complicated. If you've followed the competition for a few years, you probably remember when watching was much simpler. National broadcasters and telecom companies often held football rights and bundled matches into their TV, internet, and phone packages. That model is changing, said Thomas Peeters, a sports economist and professor at the Erasmus School of Economics. “A lot of the broadcasting rights that used to be free-to-air on one of the channels that you had anyway have been migrating to more streaming services dedicated specifically to sports.” In Germany, for example, DAZN shows all Champions League matches except the top match on Tuesday evenings, which Prime Video holds exclusively. title: Oregon Housing Leader Met With Officials Who Are Seeking Money for a Project Her Husband’s Employer Is Developing
content:
When Oregon’s Housing Stability Council met by Zoom in early October, the state’s top housing official told the oversight board that she wanted to address a story ProPublica published that morning.

The story revealed that the official, Andrea Bell, hadn’t clearly disclosed her husband’s work for a small consulting firm that helps housing authorities develop apartments, sometimes with money from Bell’s agency. Nor had she notified Gov. Tina Kotek about it, something Oregon law requires of a governor’s appointee when an actual or potential conflict arises.

Council members, who award hundreds of millions of dollars in housing subsidies, affirmed their support for Bell, who told them she wanted to be clear: “None of the projects that are coming from the council impact my household income.”

Newly obtained records, however, show a clear financial connection between the council’s decisions and her husband’s employer. The records also show that Bell was personally involved in meetings and internal discussions about state funding of a large apartment project, Aloha 209th, which her husband’s employer is helping to develop.

title: Five reasons why we should still make things with our hands
content:
It’s 7 a.m. Still dark outside. “Alex, time to wake up! You have a busy day ahead, with an important meeting at 8:30,” announces the alarm in a soft but firm voice. Alex wakes up immediately, already thinking about the presentation that still needs a few finishing touches. In the kitchen, the coffee machine, set up for 7 a.m. sharp, has just finished brewing. “Alexa, set the temperature to 20 degrees,” says Alex, reaching for the coffee. But then, something catches Alex’s attention: a little bonsai tree on the windowsill. For the next few minutes, Alex forgets about the coffee, the presentation and the meeting. Carefully trimming new shoots, removing dead leaves and checking the soil, Alex becomes completely absorbed in the task. The technology fades into the background. So does the stress.

For a few precious minutes, Alex is simply enjoying doing something with his own hands.

Whether it’s gardening, knitting, cooking or repairing an old chair, making things with our hands can do much more than produce a finished object. AI will therefore never take away this pleasure, since our fascination with making things by hand has survived centuries of technological progress.

title: Demarinaisten Marttila: Pakottava kontrolli on kriminalisoitava – ”Kyse on järjestelmällisestä vallankäytöstä”
content:
Demarinaisten puheenjohtaja, kansanedustaja Helena Marttila kannattaa pakottavan kontrollin kriminalisoimista omana rikosnimikkeenään.

Marttila ottaa asiaan kantaa kansainvälisenä naisiin kohdistuvan väkivallan vastaisena päivänä. Hän pitää tärkeänä YK:n Oranssit päivät -kampanjan suojelijana toimivan presidentin puolison Suzanne Innes-Stubbin Ilta-Sanomissa esiin nostamaa tavoitetta pakottavan kontrollin kriminalisoimisesta.

– Pakottava kontrolli ei aina jätä näkyviä jälkiä, mutta se voi viedä ihmiseltä vapauden, turvallisuuden ja mahdollisuuden tehdä omaa elämäänsä koskevia päätöksiä. Se voi näkyä eristämisenä, taloudellisena kontrollina, jatkuvana valvontana, liikkumisen rajoittamisena tai uhkailuna. Kyse ei ole tavallisista parisuhteen ristiriidoista vaan järjestelmällisestä vallankäytöstä, Marttila sanoo tiedotteessa.

Marttila pitää merkittävänä puutteena, ettei pakottavan kontrollin kriminalisointia sisällytetty hallituksen esitykseen, jolla toimeenpannaan naisiin kohdistuvan väkivallan vastainen EU-direktiivi.

title: Let the beat drop
content:
We’re officially entering low power mode, but we have a couple more stories for you to close out the week. In the impending retail spirit, I review a device that’s not a sex toy. 

You don’t really realize how much downtime there is in the song “Sandstorm” by Darude until you’re waiting for the bass to drop while it’s playing inside your vagina. 

In August 2025, I got an email with the subject line “‘Airpods for your @ss’ raises nearly half a million in Kickstarter campaign.” I get a lot of zany pitches for products that don’t exist yet, and a lot of pitches for products that do exist but perhaps should not. This one was for a device called the Groove Thing, a sex toy that turns music into vibration patterns. But the pitch didn’t include the phrase “sex toy” at all. Instead, it’s called an “internal music player.”

title: Israel/OPT: Women and girls bear the crushing toll of Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza
content:
Israel has relentlessly inflicted repeated and cumulative harms on women and girls in the occupied Gaza Strip since October 2023 as an integral part of its ongoing genocide against Palestinians, said Amnesty International in a new report published today. 

No conditions for life: Women, girls and the gendered dimensions of Israel’s genocide against Palestinians in Gaza, lays out in 135 pages of harrowing detail, Israel’s ongoing genocide despite the so-called ceasefire of October 2025, providing evidence of how the Israeli military, between 7 October 2023 and 1 October 2026, has repeatedly killed, injured, forcibly displaced, unlawfully detained, deliberately denied women and girls access to essential healthcare, including reproductive healthcare, and starved them. It illustrates how these measures have forced women into a daily struggle for survival defined by grief and trauma and stripped away the conditions necessary for women to exercise autonomy over decisions relating to pregnancy, childbirth and reproductive health.

title: Lukiolaiskysely 2026–2027: Neljännes lukiolaisista kysyy jatko-opinnoista tekoälyltä, mutta vain 8 % pitää sitä hyvin luotettavana
content:
Tekoälyn käyttö jatko-opintotiedon hakemisessa on kasvanut vuodessa 14 prosentista 26 prosenttiin, mutta luotetuimpana tiedonlähteenä lukiolaiset pitävät opinto-ohjaajia. studentum.fi selvitti kahdeksatta kertaa lukiolaisten ajatuksia jatko-opinnoista, tiedonhausta ja opiskeluvalinnoista.

Lukiolaiset hakevat tietoa jatko-opinnoista tekoälyn avulla yhä useammin, mutta luottamus ei kasva samaa vauhtia. Lukiolaisista neljännes käyttää tekoälyä opiskelumahdollisuuksien selvittämiseen, kun viime vuonna osuus oli 14 %. Yleisimmät tiedonhaun kanavat ovat kuitenkin hakukoneet (86 %), Opintopolku.fi (58 %) ja sosiaalinen media (51 %).

Tekoälyyn luottaa jonkin verran 53 % lukiolaisista (viime vuonna 48 %), mutta hyvin luotettavana sitä pitää vain 8 % (viime vuonna 7 %). Opinto-ohjaajat ovat edelleen luotetuin tiedonlähde: heitä pitää hyvin luotettavina 83 %.

Opiskelupaikan valinnassa tärkeintä on edelleen kiinnostava ala (75 %). Hyvät työllistymismahdollisuudet (49 %) ovat nyt kuitenkin tärkeämpi valintakriteeri kuin hyvät palkkanäkymät (43 %). Viime vuonna järjestys oli päinvastainen.

title: EU Commission wants €50B fund to keep tech European
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission is planning to take direct stakes worth hundreds of millions of euros in homegrown tech companies to keep them European, according to a plan unveiled Wednesday.

The Sovereign Tech Equity Fund has an envisioned size of €50 billion. Public money from the EU, member countries and partners such as the European Investment Bank will aim to draw in private capital to invest in critical technologies.

The goal is to fund tech that is essential to the bloc’s “technological sovereignty and economic security,” a Commission official told reporters, granted anonymity to discuss details of the plan ahead of its formal presentation.

“We need to use public funding more efficiently as a catalyst to crowd in private capital,” the official added.

The announcement comes two weeks after the EU leaders’ first-ever meeting on AI, where European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen promised to come up with a funding proposal for the EU to become less reliant on U.S. or Chinese technology. The broader investment plan would need about €500 billion, according to Commission estimates.

title: Muutos tulee, se on varma – Kylvö-kirja tuo toivoa monikriisin ratkaisuun
content:
Liisa Vähäkylä

Kylvö eli Kirja mullasta, vallasta ja huomispäivän ruoasta esittelee ruuantuotantoon liittyviä kohtuuttomuuksia ja kartoittaa suunnitelmia, joita yksilöillä ja yhteisöillä on haavoittuneen ruokajärjestelmän muuttamiseksi.

Kun yhä pienempi, iäkkäämpi ja velkaantuneempi joukko tuottaa yhä enemmän ruokaa, tämä on alkanut näkyä elintarvikkeiden laadussa. Koska ruuan heikko laatu lisää ihmisten sairauksia, asialle on tehtävä jotain. Pahimmillaan ruoka loppuu kaupoista.

Tietokirjalla on neljä tekijää, joista kolme on itsenäisiä reporttereita ja neljäs kuvajournalisti.

Hanna Nikkanen tunnetaan useaan otteeseen palkittuna ympäristöjournalistina ja yhtenä Long Play -verkkolehden perustajana, joka piipahti Tampereen yliopistossa työelämäprofessorina lukuvuonna 2016–17. Läheinen yhteistyö opiskelijoiden kanssa on aiemmin poikinut monia journalistisia hankkeita.

Kirjoittajista Johannes Roviomaa on Nikkasen opiskelija. Hän on kirjoittanut kolumneja Ylen verkkosivuille sekä Ylioppilaslehteen ja työskentelee vierailevana tutkijana Lapin yliopiston Arktisessa keskuksessa. Siellä hänen erikoistumisalueenaan on pohjoisen alueen ilmasto-olosuhteet sekä ilmastonkorjaus.

title: Documenting Uzbekistan Through Wikimedia Commons: My Journey as a Contributor
content:
Wikimedia Commons plays an important role in preserving and sharing freely licensed photographs,videos and other media with people around the world. For me, it has also become a way to document Uzbekistan, Uzbek people, sporting achievements and everyday life.

I began contributing to Wikimedia Commons in October 2014. Over the years my interests and activities have developed, but one objective has remained important: making useful visual material about Uzbekistan more accessible to everyone.

As of November 2026, I have uploaded 1,424 files to Wikimedia Commons.

One of my main areas of interest is Uzbek football. Football is an important part of the country’s sporting and cultural life; yet many Uzbek footballers, clubs, stadiums and sporting events remain under represented in freely accessible visual collections.

Through my contributions, I have tried to help fill this gap.

My uploads include photographs of Uzbek footballers, teams, stadiums and football-related events.

I have also contributed photographs of stadiums and teams from different levels of Uzbek football.

title: US Plans to Cut Off Iran’s Caspian Lifeline
content:
US Central Command announced a plan on November 8 to block Iran’s land-based supply lines, building on its months-long naval blockade of the Islamic Republic’s ports. The goal of Task Force Iron Gate is to prevent Tehran from using alternative routes to transport advanced weapons, dual-use materials, and energy products.

Since the US and Israel started an all-out war on Iran in February and subsequently blockaded the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran has increasingly looked to northern corridors, particularly through Russia, to maintain access to foreign markets and critical supplies. The shift has elevated the importance of the Caspian route and forced Washington to take additional measures. 

Despite on-again, off-again negotiations between the US, Iran and intermediaries seeking to end the war, which has rattled global markets and sent inflation soaring. There is little sign of a resolution.

While Tehran has been able to rely primarily on its domestic defense industry for weapons production, it is increasingly looking to the north for imports, with the Caspian corridor emerging as a key route for defense-related procurement and logistical support.

title: Billions in EU funds are vanishing – Brussels wants to rewrite the rules
content:
The European Parliament is calling for closer cooperation between the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF), the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) and national authorities, while the European Commission is considering a common data-sharing system, the use of artificial intelligence and new analytical tools.

The debate over the EU’s anti-fraud architecture is linked to preparations for the bloc’s next budget, covering the period from 2028 to 2034. The European Commission has proposed a multiannual financial framework worth €1.98tn. Under the new model, payments would be increasingly tied to performance and the achievement of milestones.

European Commission figures illustrate the scale of the problem. In 2024, it recorded 13,589 irregularities involving EU funds, including both suspected cases of fraud and non-fraudulent irregularities. Their combined financial value amounted to €1.84bn.

title: An Alarming Spike in Ectopic Pregnancy Deaths Was Hiding in Plain Sight in a Federal Dataset
content:
For years, ProPublica has examined maternal health and the ongoing impacts of abortion bans since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade. Data analysis has been central to that effort, offering a quantitative view into an area that has long been underresearched, especially as studying the impact of abortion bans has become politicized and federal agencies have been gutted under the Trump administration.

For example, last year my colleagues uncovered a dramatic rise in sepsis rates since Texas instituted its abortion ban, which carries the strictest penalties for healthcare providers. The number of blood transfusions during emergency room visits for first-trimester miscarriage spiked in the state as well. 

Most recently, my colleagues Andrea Suozzo, Sophie Chou, Kavitha Surana and I examined pregnancy-related deaths on a national level. We turned our attention to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data. The agency collects information from death certificates and publishes totals based on variables like location, demographics and cause of death. It’s a commonly used resource for journalists and academics who want to learn more about trends in mortality.

title: Is AI-assisted thinking devaluing business degrees?
content:
As AI models improve, high-quality knowledge is becoming easier to access. A degree therefore has to certify something more durable than the ability to retrieve knowledge or produce a plausible answer. It must show that a student can exercise judgement, make decisions and defend them.

Since mid-September, high-school students across France, joined by university students, have blocked schools and taken to the streets to protest the conditions in which they study. Their demands include more staff, shorter school days, smaller classes, better-maintained buildings and the reform or abolition of Parcoursup, the admissions platform they regard as opaque and unfair. These grievances stand on their own, and they are not about artificial intelligence. But they do raise questions that every school in France, including mine, will have to confront.

title: Juko: Velkajarru ei saa muuttua julkisen sektorin palkkajarruksi
content:
Julkisalan koulutettujen neuvottelujärjestön Jukon hallituksen puheenjohtaja Katarina Murto vaatii rajoja julkisen sektorin säästöille.

Jukon puheenjohtajan mukaan valtiontalouden heikot näkymät ja jatkuvat säästötoimet kasvattavat julkisella sektorilla henkilöstöön kohdistuvaa tehostamista ja lisäävät työpaikoilla epävarmuutta.

Hänen mukaansa kansantalouden vaikea tilanne tuo suuria haasteita vuoden 2028 neuvottelukierrokselle, jolloin nykyiset julkisalojen työ- ja virkaehtosopimukset päättyvät.

– Velkajarrunkaan oloissa yleisen linjan alittaminen ei ole vaihtoehto, Murto sanoi tiedotteen mukaan Jukon liittokokouksessa keskiviikkona.

Opetusalan ammattijärjestö OAJ:n sekä Jukon puheenjohtajana toimiva Murto huomauttaa, että velkajarrusta huolimatta säästämisellä on rajansa.

– Velkajarru ei saa muuttua julkisen sektorin palkka- tai hyvinvointijarruksi. Emme voi hyväksyä lähtökohdaksi väitettä, että julkinen sektori olisi yksiselitteisesti liian kallis ja tehoton.

Murron mielestä toimintaa pitää uudistaa, turhaa työtä vähentää ja tekoälyä hyödyntää.

title: I Listened to ‘Sandstorm’ Through a Sex Toy
content:
You don’t really realize how much downtime there is in the song “Sandstorm” by Darude until you’re waiting for the bass to drop while it’s playing inside your vagina. 

In August 2025, I got an email with the subject line “‘Airpods for your @ss’ raises nearly half a million in Kickstarter campaign.” I get a lot of zany pitches for products that don’t exist yet, and a lot of pitches for products that do exist but perhaps should not. This one was for a device called the Groove Thing, a sex toy that turns music into vibration patterns. But the pitch didn’t include the phrase “sex toy” at all. Instead, it’s called an “internal music player.” 

I asked for a unit to review, expecting this to be purely conceptual. But they had one, and offered to send it. “The prototype functions very similarly to the final product but we do want to stress it’s a garage built prototype,” the rep for Groove Thing told me. I thought for a moment about putting something “garage built” and connected to a wall outlet into an orifice and passed. While others were braver, I decided to wait until the version they planned to send to customers in the fall was ready.

title: SICSS Ouagadougou 2026: When Wikimedia Meets Computational Social Sciences in Francophone Africa
content:
From August 10 to 21, 2026, Ouagadougou, the capital of Burkina Faso, hosted the second edition of the Summer School in Computational Social Sciences (SICSS). Two days were devoted to Wikipedia, Wikidata, and open data, which were presented not only as platforms for contributing to content creation but also as sources of structured data for the study, analysis, and understanding of society.

What happens when researchers think of Wikipedia and Wikidata not only as sources of knowledge, but also as data that can help us better understand society ?

It was precisely this question that guided Wikimedia’s activities during the Summer Institute in Computational Social Sciences (SICSS 2026). SICSS is an international network of summer schools dedicated to computational methods in the social sciences. The 2026 session took place from August 10 to 21 at the Higher Institute of Population Sciences (ISSP) at Joseph Ki-Zerbo University in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. It was made possible thanks to the support of Wiki In Africa, funded by the Wikimedia Foundation’s research fund.

title: AI’s Back Door to Finance
content:
Imagine asking an AI assistant to find you a better mortgage, compare your pension investments, and move your savings to an account offering a higher return. With your permission, it examines your finances, identifies better deals, and acts. No forms, no lengthy comparisons, no switching between banking apps. Just a digital assistant working in your financial interests.

This is the promise of agentic AI: technology that can make decisions and carry out tasks, making financial services more innovative, competitive, and affordable. There is one major obstacle: access to financial data.

In its 2027 work program, the European Commission announced plans to withdraw its proposed Financial Data Access Regulation (FIDA). FIDA represented Europe’s ambitious attempt to open up financial data beyond banking, allowing customers to give third parties access to their savings, investment, insurance, and pension accounts.

AI is already transforming personal finance. In the US, OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, and Google’s Gemini permit consumers to connect with their financial accounts and ask questions about their finances. Although these services have yet to launch in Europe, they are coming.

title: False Claims That Romania, Poland and Bulgaria Will Leave NATO in 2027 Spread Online
content:
“Romania, Poland, Lithuania, Turkey and Bulgaria will leave NATO at V. Putin’s request starting in 2027” was the headline of a disinformation narrative widely shared on TikTok and Facebook. One of the individuals spreading the false claim works for Bucharest’s District 2 City Hall.

The post also claims that US President Donald Trump has accepted Putin’s conditions and that former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán will take over the leadership in Brussels.

Other versions of the story claim that the decisions were made by Trump, Xi and Putin.

Commenters have welcomed the supposed development, with very few questioning how the Russian president could possibly have a say in whether a country leaves NATO.

On Reddit, reactions have been more balanced, with users questioning what Romania could possibly gain from such a decision, particularly given the current regional security situation.

Why is this narrative false?

title: Voting rights for AI? The research behind an unsettling idea
content:
AI researchers are giving increasing attention to the idea of AI models becoming conscious. The implications are potentially huge: a conscious AI model would no longer be a tool we can use as we wish, but a being with moral status and interests of its own. If AI also became capable of moral agency, it might one day have a claim to political voice.

Critics, however, dismiss the prospect as an illusion and question the motives of the commercial labs investigating it. Others have sought to settle the matter by declaration. The Vatican says AI systems lack conscious experience, while lawmakers in Ohio have proposed declaring them nonsentient.

But research into AI consciousness does not mean any system already is conscious or could soon be. It is also easy to confuse the different capacities relevant to moral status, and to presume that the problem of consciousness in AI can be legislated away.

Part of my new book, Recoding Democracy: AI and the Fight for Our Democratic Future, tries to disentangle these confusions. It also asks what, if anything, could give AI a right to vote, and whether these questions deserve serious attention at all.

title: Pourquoi certains pays réussissent-ils mieux leur transition énergétique que d’autres ?
content:
La transition énergétique est souvent présentée comme une affaire de technologies, de réglementations ou de financements. Pourtant, un facteur plus discret pourrait expliquer pourquoi certains pays avancent plus vite que d’autres : leur culture nationale.

Depuis une quinzaine d’années, les obligations vertes se sont imposées comme l’un des instruments phares de la finance durable. Elles permettent de financer des projets d’énergies renouvelables, de mobilité propre ou d’efficacité énergétique. Leur essor spectaculaire témoigne de la mobilisation croissante des marchés financiers face à l’urgence climatique. Mais une question demeure : pourquoi ces financements semblent-ils accélérer la transition dans certains pays, alors que leur impact reste plus limité dans d’autres ?

Notre recherche montre que les différences ne tiennent pas seulement aux politiques publiques ou au niveau de développement économique. Elles s’expliquent aussi par les valeurs et les comportements collectifs propres à chaque société.

title: Treasury CIO Is Vibe Coding a ‘Civilization’ Clone During Treasury Department Hack
content:
As the Treasury Department dealt with the fallout of a hack that took down some of its services, its Chief Information Officer was pushing updates to Legatum, his vibe coded Civilization clone.

Sam Corcos is the cofounder of the A16z-backed glucose monitoring health startup called Levels; he became the Treasury Department’s Chief Information Officer as a DOGE hire near the beginning of Trump’s second term, and has been a leading AI evangelist within the administration since. Corcos’s department is in charge of cybersecurity for the Treasury Department, and so it is possibly concerning that while the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) is dealing with a “cybersecurity incident” that has taken a critical bank compliance reporting panel down, he has been actively pushing balance patches, new theme music for the Aztec faction, and critical tweaks to the in-game player assistance tooltips for Legatum, his vibe-coded “turn-based strategy game in the tradition of Civilization VI.”

title: Too Big to Fire? Jensen Huang Is Back at Nvidia; Questions Loom Over AI Boom & U.S.-China Relations
content:
Nvidia stock prices surged over 30% on Monday as the chip maker reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Huang had stepped down earlier in November amid reports he had multiple extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China. Huang and Nvidia have been central to the AI boom, and the leadership turmoil had erased trillions in value from the U.S. stock market. President Donald Trump acknowledged he had encouraged the company’s board to bring Huang back.

“The fact that our markets are so over-indexed on the AI trade, that something like three-fourths of gains in the S&P 500 this past year have been AI-related, is unsustainable,” says Aya Ibrahim, senior fellow for economic and national security at the AI Now Institute.

“The relationship is beside the point. The issue here is we have one man, one firm that many people, including those in our government, now believe are indispensable both to our economic growth and stability and to national security.”

British and Irish Sound Archives (BISA) invites proposals for presentations at

The two-day conference will feature presentations, practical sessions and
collaborative discussions, as well as the BISA Annual General Meeting.

We welcome proposals on any aspect of working in the sound heritage field. As
we will be celebrating our 20th anniversary in 2026, we’re interested in hearing
from archivists, engineers, researchers and other sound archives and creative
practitioners interested in reflecting on changes to practice, technology, and
research use that have taken place over the last two decades.

Previous delegates have also expressed an interest in the following aspects of
sound archive work and research: digitisation and digital preservation;
cataloguing; access and re-use; copyright and data protection; fundraising and
advocacy; and AI.

title: Australian Billionaire Politician Clive Palmer and His Wanted Nephew Had Vanuatu Diplomatic Passports
content:
Australian billionaire politician Clive Palmer, along with his wife and nephew, received diplomatic passports and appointments from Vanuatu, according to a parliamentary report in the Pacific nation.

Vanuatu’s Public Accounts Committee recently released a report into the issuance of diplomatic passports by officials. Among more than two dozen cancelled diplomatic passports listed in an appendix to the report, OCCRP found Palmer and his two family members.

Palmer was appointed as a Vanuatu trade commissioner on May 29, 2023. Two months earlier, on March 17, Vanuatu gave a similar posting to his nephew, Clive Mensink — who was wanted by Australian authorities at the time for contempt of court in a case about a corporate collapse.

Palmer’s wife, Anna, was made a Vanuatu trade commissioner at the same time as her husband.

All three had their diplomatic passports cancelled in September of 2025, the appendix shows, as Vanuatu cracked down on the issuance of such documents to foreign and dual citizens.

“Mr. Palmer was invited to be an ambassador to the previous Vanuatu Government because of his experience in international trade,” said Andrew Crook, a spokesman for the billionaire.
snippet: Australian billionaire politician Clive Palmer, along with his wife and nephew, received diplomatic passports and appointments from Vanuatu, according to a parliamentary report in the Pacific nation.

title: How a Public Radio Project Turned the Public Domain Into a Creative Playground
content:
Simon Close says The Public Song Project invites people to think of the public domain as a free archive. It’s a place where creative works from the past can be adapted and reimagined through the eyes of new artists.

Close is a producer for WNYC public radio in New York City and host of the Public Song Project, now in its fourth year. The station partnered with the Internet Archive for the 2026 contest, which he said expanded the horizons of the project and helped boost entries to a new record surpassing 200 submissions.

“We’ve gotten some real experienced pros who make music their professional lives, and also people who came across the project and just like to be creative or have some emotional attachment to the song that they chose to cover,” Close said. “This year we had way more submissions from different parts of the country and, more thrilling, from all over the world.”

title: Kremlin Campaign to Crush Kaliningrad’s Identity
content:
Kaliningrad Regional Court sentenced lawyer and human rights defender Maria Bontsler to 12 years in prison for treason on November 12, after she was accused of passing information to Ukrainian intelligence. Bontsler’s real crime has been defending local people from political prosecutions.

The verdict was the latest step in a two-decade campaign to ensure Kaliningrad, Russia’s westernmost territory, has no independent political life.

For NATO planners, the exclave is a problem of missile ranges and the Suwałki Gap, the narrow strip on the border between Poland and Lithuania which links Kaliningrad to Belarus. For the Kremlin, weaponization of the territory is made easier by the absence of any civic movement that questions it.

It wasn’t always this way. Back in 1993, Sergey Pasko founded the Baltic Republican Party (BRP), which had influence beyond its list of barely 500 formal members.

title: Strengthening gender-inclusive mediation in an era of global uncertainty
content:
For three days, mediators, peacebuilding experts, diplomats and researchers from around the world gathered in Oslo to explore a pressing question: how can peace processes remain gender-inclusive and effective in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical landscape?

From 17–19 November, the UN High-Level Seminar on Gender and Inclusive Mediation Strategies brought together experts to share lessons, strengthen skills and examine current challenges facing peace mediation today.

Participants at the 15th UN High-Level Seminar on Gender and Peace Mediation Strategies in Oslo. PRIO / Cendi Frydenlund

Participants engaged in sessions covering gender-sensitive conflict analysis, mediation process design, conflict-related sexual violence, women’s participation in negotiations, peace agreement provisions and implementation challenges. The discussions took place against a backdrop of growing international tensions and increasing pressure on multilateral norms.

title: Telling Stories under Oppression: The Power of Textiles in Chile
content:
A powerful illustration of how stories can be told in empowering and engaging ways are arpilleras. Arpilleras are three-dimensional, hand-sewn appliquéd tapestries that “tell a story with each stitch”. They originated in Chile as a medium for women, generally working collectively, to denounce the human rights abuses and repression of the Pinochet dictatorship in Chile.

They have since been used to capture the first-person, lived experience of individuals and communities around the world, in response to war and conflict, and a wide range of other forms of oppression and social injustice.

title: Sanctions against Russia are working, but shadow fleet and weapons’ production expose weaknesses
content:
Sanctions are having an effect, but their effectiveness is undermined by inconsistent enforcement, insufficient cooperation between countries and opportunities to circumvent the restrictions.

Why do gaps in the sanctions’ system persist, and what needs to change to ensure that sanctions achieve their intended goals? These questions were discussed by experts and representatives of national authorities at the Financial Intelligence Unit’s (FIU) eighth annual international sanctions conference, The Impact of Sanctions: Undermining Russia’s War Capabilities.

In October, the Council of the European Union adopted a decision to significantly expand its sanctions lists against Russia, imposing additional restrictive measures on more than 1,600 individuals and legal entities. This was the largest single expansion of individual EU sanctions imposed in response to Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine to date.

The sanctions targeted:

  • 826 companies;
  • 743 individuals;
  • 77 individuals involved in organising the illegal “elections”.

title: In Bulgaria, blood is a family affair
content: “When you pass by the hospital, a man will ask whether you need blood. In 2021, I paid 400 leva (€200) for a unit of blood,” said Hristo (not his real name) from Pernik, Bulgaria. Every day, around 600 Bulgarians need blood donations following accidents, surgeries, or chronic illnesses. Yet under Bulgarian law selling blood is illegal. In 2025, Bulgaria had 182,154 blood donors, according to Pencho Penchev, head of health policy at the Bulgarian Red Cross. That was an increase of about 2.5% from the previous year. Still, only 24 out of every 1,000 citizens donate blood. One reason for the shortfall is Bulgaria's so-called “family model”, under which patients rely on relatives to donate blood. These donations account for 85%-90% of the country's total blood supply. But what happens when you have a rare blood group and none of your relatives can donate? You go outside the hospital, where the dealer – often from the Roma community – offers to pose as a “relative” and donate his blood in exchange for a few hundred euros. “With rare blood types, you have no other choice” continued Hristo. title: A Startup Tied to Donald Trump Jr. Could Get a Historic $15 Billion Loan From the Pentagon
content:
In what would rank among the largest government loans in U.S. history, the Pentagon is considering extending $15 billion to a California-based startup with financial ties to Donald Trump Jr., according to interviews and records reviewed by ProPublica.

The award would be one of the biggest the federal government has given to a firm connected to the Trump family and would go to a defense contractor with a largely untested track record.

The startup, Hadrian Automation, has attracted over a billion dollars in private investment in recent months on the promise that it can build factories that use AI and robots to more efficiently produce precision components for defense, aerospace and other industries.

If approved, the loan would be almost twice the value of the entire company, based on estimates from a round of financing this summer. Hadrian announced that round of investment included “major participation by 1789 Capital,” the venture capital firm that Trump Jr. joined as a partner after his father was elected in November 2024. 1789 also invested in the company in 2025.

title: Smartphones transform prison journalism. The FCC wants to jam them
content:
For most of society, the smartphone is just an ordinary part of modern life. But inside prisons like the one in Texas where I reside, that same technology fundamentally alters the balance of information and power.

Prison officials know this well, and they’ve collaborated with Brendan Carr’s Federal Communications Commission to allow cellphone jammers in state prisons. The FCC passed the initiative last week, although it’s up to states whether to participate.

Officials, of course, claim that the effort is needed to stop incarcerated people from coordinating crimes with those on the outside using contraband cellphones. But I strongly suspect that it’s really about censorship.

For the skeptical: Does anyone think those advocating for cellphone jamming would allow every incarcerated person a video camera instead of a cellphone? We all know the answer, and, if we’re being honest with ourselves, we know why.

The smartphone, labeled illegal contraband by prison officials, allows an incarcerated individual to completely circumvent institutional control designed to prevent those in its custody from accessing modern information ecosystems and documenting abuses.

In October and November 2026, Kyrgyzstan’s president, Sadyr Japarov, held public meetings with the population in all seven provinces of the country. What were meant to be formal events turned into quests for justice by people driven to desperation.

The meetings revealed the ineffectiveness of the existing justice mechanisms and showed how people saw the president as the only guarantor of justice.

title: A Christmas Carol for Capitalists? Dickens, Capra, and the Limits of Redemption
content:
By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 24 November 2026 (IDN) — Ebenezer, the newest film adaptation of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol, stars Johnny Depp in the eponymous role of Scrooge. The film has been called a “Christmas Carol for Capitalists” by David Crow, writing in Den of Geek—presumably because the poor are portrayed as dishonest, taking advantage of the well-off through fraudulent means, while those who seem to be acting on behalf of the poor are in reality lining their pockets with the charity of others. Or, like the unfortunate and generous-hearted Mr. Fezziwig, they wind up knifed to death by one of the underclass—a gratuitous act of violence, perhaps, and one not to be found in Dickens’ original story.

title: Valtiota on vaikea rakentaa, ellei hoida ensin omia traumojaan, sanoo Rowda Olad
content:
Kun Rowda Olad palasi kotimaahansa Somaliaan vuonna 2016, hänellä oli suuria suunnitelmia. Hän aikoi perustaa maahan mielenterveysklinikan.  

Olad oli paennut maan sisällissotaa Yhdysvaltoihin lapsena ja mennyt yliopistoon. Pääaineeksi oli valikoitunut psykologia. Syynä oli se, että hän oli vieraillut Somaliassa muutamaa vuotta ennen paluutaan ja nähnyt, millä tolalla maan mielenterveyspalvelut olivat. 

Mielisairaaloita oli vain yksi, eikä sillä ollut riittävää kapasiteettia hoitaa potilaitaan. Monissa perheissä potilaat vain sidottiin paikalleen tai heitä yritettiin hoitaa perinteisten parannusmenetelmien avulla.

Maan olosuhteet olivat kuitenkin rauhoittuneet, ja Olad halusi osallistua valtion jälleenrakentamiseen avaamalla mielisairaalan.

”Sitten tajusin, ettei ammattilaisia ollut saatavilla eikä minulla olisi henkilökuntaa. Olen vain yksi ihminen. Sairaalan tai klinikan perustamisessa ei olisi järkeä.” 

Pian paluunsa jälkeen hän kiinnostuikin yksittäisten potilaiden hoitamisen sijaan siitä, miten mielenterveysongelmat vaikuttavat Somaliaan laajemmin: miten ne vaikeuttavat valtion instituutioiden rakentamista ja sisäisten konfliktien ratkaisemista.

title: Advancing M20 calls: Networks push EU on AI copyright and cloud safeguards
content:
Two global digital media networks have called on the European Union to include independent journalism in its push for digital sovereignty.

In two submissions to the European Commission in November, the EU is urged to confront Big Tech’s growing control over both the digital infrastructure journalists depend on and the news content AI companies use to build their products.

Together, the submissions argue that Europe’s digital sovereignty agenda must address both sides of the problem: who controls the infrastructure that delivers information;  and who controls — and profits from — the journalism that makes it valuable.

The submissions urge the EU to invest in independent, public-interest cloud infrastructure while strengthening copyright protections to prevent dominant AI companies from exploiting publishers’ work without fair compensation.
snippet: Two global digital media networks have called on the European Union to include independent journalism in its push for digital sovereignty.

title: Climate summits need radical reform – here’s how to transform global negotiations
content:
The recent failure of the UN climate summit, Cop31, went beyond already gloomy expectations. Yet this political and diplomatic catastrophe may become a historical opportunity for global climate governance to tackle its structural problems.

It is a miracle that Cop climate summits have survived and grown for 31 years, with all decisions needing unanimous consensus from all 195 nations or parties. Cops have produced some positive results such as the 2015 Paris climate agreement to cut greenhouse gases. But now it’s time for radical reform. A reform that must not only abolish unanimity, but also make the Cop capable of engaging a strong enough coalition of interests to advance the climate change agenda.

Where could that start? What kind of alliance does such a reform need? A recent conference on the global governance of climate change provides some answers.

title: Justice is elusive for the Rohingya even after the ICJ’s landmark genocide ruling against Myanmar
content:
By nine votes to six, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya people in connection with its 2017 “clearance operations” in Rakhine State. The ruling is an alarm bell for all states accused of genocide.

The year 2017 was not the first Rohingya exodus from Myanmar: in 1978 and again in 1991-92, hundreds of thousands of Rohingya poured into Bangladesh to escape state persecution. Many returned, and were forced to flee again when new violence erupted.

Today, more than 1.2 million Rohingya are in refugee camps in Bangladesh without any concrete prospect to return to Myanmar. Most Rohingya want to return, but not without conditions that would ensure their safety. The most crucial condition is the guarantee of citizenship rights.

Since Myanmar stripped the Rohingya of their citizenship in 1982, they have been living under apartheid-like conditions. Among many discriminatory policies imposed on Rohingya life, the Rohingya faced restrictions on movement, education and health care while families were restricted to a two-child limit. Returning to Myanmar just to face the same conditions of life is not an option for many Rohingya.
snippet: By nine votes to six, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya people in connection with its 2017 “clearance operations” in Rakhine
creator: San Beauchemin, Doctoral Researcher, School of Political Studies, L’Université d’Ottawa/University of Ottawa

title: Diluted, abandoned...but it's not all bad news
content:
It’s six years since we got together with Climate Emergency UK to build CAPE, gathering together data on local councils’ climate commitments and plans.

Back then, we listed 328 councils who’d declared a climate emergency, and over the years we’ve kept up to date with which councils have published a plan and a date for reaching net zero, either in their own operations or across their region as a whole —
337 in all.

But times change, and the intervening years have seen some unexpected developments. It’s far from a straight line from a council making a climate pledge to reaching net zero carbon emissions, and we’ve seen target dates set back, pledges diluted, and in some cases, abandoned all together.

It's not all bad news, though: more councils have brought their net zero date forward or extended their ambitions than otherwise. It's a complicated picture — “a patchwork of commitments that create a postcode lottery on climate action”, as Climate Emergency UK’s Isaac Beevor says.

title: Can we play our way to better research data?
content:
Research data management and open science are important. But that does not mean they always have to be taught through another presentation, another checklist, or another hour of definitions.

What if researchers could solve a mystery, build with LEGO®, escape from a locked room, investigate persistent identifiers, or make decisions about the future of research data instead? There is a surprisingly creative world of games designed to do exactly that.

Many research data management topics are easier to understand when participants have to make decisions themselves.

  • Should this dataset be preserved?
  • Which metadata are actually necessary?
  • What happens when important information is missing?
  • Can this material legally be reused?
  • Which persistent identifier belongs to which research object?
  • And what consequences can today’s publishing decision have several years from now?
snippet: Research data management and open science are important. But that does not mean they always have to be taught through another presentation, another checklist, or another hour of definitions.

title: Europe: Judgments on ‘instrumentalization’ of migration a devastating blow to the absolute prohibition of torture
content:
Today, the European Court of Human Rights ruled on cases of summary forced returns at the borders of Latvia, Lithuania and Poland with Belarus, also known as pushbacks, in cases of “instrumentalization of migration” defined by the Court as the actions of a state encouraging, facilitating or forcing migration with the aim of destabilizing another state.

The Court found that summary returns at the border in this context constitute a violation of the prohibition of torture only where applicants showed “evident personal vulnerabilities” or were able to demonstrate a real and immediate threat to life or risk of ill-treatment. Reacting to the judgments, Mandi Mudarikwa, Head of Strategic Litigation at Amnesty International said:

“These rulings strike a devastating blow to legal certainty and the protection of human rights at the borders under the European Convention of Human Rights. They limit the absolute protections guaranteed under the Convention only to people who are able to show evident vulnerabilities or that they are at immediate risk. This is despite the Convention entrenching such rights, such as the prohibition of torture, as absolute and the Court itself recognizing this fact.
