title: "A Shameful Failure": U.N. Climate Summit Collapses as Final Text Drops Mention of Fossil Fuels
content:
The United Nations climate summit in Turkey, known as COP31, collapsed on Sunday after nations failed to reach an agreement on a new climate deal. A number of countries opposed the final draft because it made no mention of fossil fuels. Many poorer countries also objected to the lack of financial commitments from richer nations to assist them in adapting to the climate crisis.

“This is not about the Global South begging for assistance and help,” says Filipino climate activist Lidy Nacpil. “The principle is that [wealthy nations] have created this problem, and they have to contribute to the solutions.”

“What we’ve seen over the past decades is the Global North are not delivering on any of their responsibilities,” says Brandon Wu, director of policy and campaigns at ActionAid USA. “That’s what’s causing the deadlock. It’s not new to this COP, but it’s becoming increasingly untenable.”

We also speak with two other leading climate justice advocates who attended COP31, Tasneem Essop of Climate Action Network International and Kathy Jetn̄il-Kijiner, climate envoy of the Marshall Islands.

title: Azerbaijan Further Tightens Grip on Civil Society
content:
Azerbaijan’s parliament on November 18 approved sweeping amendments to legislation governing nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) that would expand government powers to suspend and dissolve independent groups, impose new registration requirements, and further restrict their operations. The following day, a court sentenced prominent rights defender Bashir Suleymanli to seven and a half years in prison, the latest in a series of harsh sentences against civil society activists prosecuted over foreign funding. 

The proposed legislation would allow authorities, rather than courts, to suspend NGOs for up to a year for broadly defined violations, including failure to meet transparency and anti-money laundering requirements. It would also expand grounds for court-ordered dissolution to include activities deemed a threat to the “legally protected interests of the state and society”—vague standards open to abuse.

title: How Isaac Newton Lost $3 Million Dollars in the “South Sea Bubble” of 1720: Even Geniuses Can’t Prevail Against the Machinations of the Markets
content:
The Aristotelian notion of “man” as a “rational animal” has seen its share of detractors, from the Cynics to Bertrand Russell to nearly the whole of Poststructuralist thought. Leave it up to Oscar Wilde to compress the debate between intellect and passion into a pithy aphorism: “Man is a rational animal who always loses his temper when he is called upon to act in accordance with the dictates of reason.”

We no longer need clever verbal barbs to refute too-optimistic assessments of human behavior. Economics is catching up: we have the language of neuroscience and psychology, which consistently tells us that humans decidedly do not behave rationally very often, but are driven by bias and biology in inexplicable ways. And for over a hundred years now, we’ve known that the clockwork Newtonian view of the physical universe turns out to be a much messier and indeterminate affair, as does the universe of the human mind.

title: Ilmastokokouksessa myös edistystä – saastuttavien alojen maksut saivat tukea
content:
Vaikka Antalyassa järjestetyssä YK:n ilmastokokouksessa ei saatu päätöslauselmaa aikaan, solidaarisuusmaksujen asettaminen ilmastonmuutoksen tuhojen kompensointiin liikahti eteenpäin. Joukko maita, mukana Britannia ja Espanja, allekirjoittivat julkilausuman, joka koskee pieniä, kohdennettuja maksuja saastuttaville toimialoille. Tällä halutaan saada tietyt sektorit osallistumaan enemmän ilmastotoimien kustannuksiin, kirjoittaa The Guardian.

Saastuttaja maksaa -periaatetta edistävän julkilausuman ovat tähän mennessä allekirjoittaneet myös Kenia, Etelä-Sudan, Espanja, Itä-Timor, Tuvalu ja Vanuatu.

Vaikka globaaleja solidaarisuusmaksuja ei ole vielä otettu käyttöön, Ranskan hallituksen tukema työryhmä on ehdottanut mahdollisiksi tulonlähteiksi pientä maksua eniten lentävien ja bisnesluokan matkustajien lennoille sekä maksuja kryptovaluuttakaupoille.

Viime vuonna julkaistu hollantilaisanalyysi osoitti, että lentolippuihin kohdistuva maksu tuottaisi noin 106 miljardia euroa vuodessa. Maksu alkaisi turistiluokan lyhyen matkan lennoilla 10 eurosta ja nousisi pitkän matkan lennoilla 30 euroon, kun taas bisnesluokassa se olisi lyhyillä lennoilla 20 euroa ja pitkillä 120 euroa.

title: Kehitysyhteistyö edistää Suomen turvallisuutta, kauppaa ja kansainvälistä vaikutusvaltaa
content:
Kehityspolitiikka on vahvistanut merkittävästi suomalaisen osaamisen, yritysten ja julkisten toimijoiden asemaa kansainvälisessä yhteistyössä sekä tukenut Suomen ulko- ja turvallisuuspoliittisia tavoitteita. Tämä käy ilmi vuosia 2023–2026 koskevasta kehityspolitiikan tulosraportista.

Raportin mukaan suomalainen toimijuus on vahvistunut laajasti. Suomalaiset valtiolliset toimijat, yritykset, kansalaisjärjestöt ja oppilaitokset ovat mukana yhä useammissa kansainvälisissä hankkeissa. Suomalainen osaaminen on erityisen kysyttyä digitalisaation, koulutuksen, verotuksen, kriittisten raaka-aineiden, kiertotalouden ja hyvän hallinnon teemoissa.

Erityisen huomattava muutos on tapahtunut suomalaisten toteuttaman EU:n kansainvälisen yhteistyön volyymissa, joka on 17-kertaistunut hallituskauden aikana. Tämä luo mahdollisuuksia suomalaisille julkisen sektorin toimijoille ja sitä kautta laajemmin yrityksille ja muille tahoille. Samalla Suomen näkyvyys EU:n ulkosuhteissa on vahvistunut.

title: Taking down the old Serbia
content: For as long as I can remember, Vojislav Šešelj's face has looked down over Novi Sad, Serbia's second-largest city. A giant poster of his head stood on one of the city’s central boulevards, despite years of protests and complaints. Šešelj leads the far-right Serbian Radical Party, and the UN war crimes tribunal in The Hague convicted him of crimes against humanity in 2018. He was also a long-standing political ally of Vučić's ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), and a prominent figure on the Serbian nationalist right since the 1990s. The poster carried a message denying the Srebrenica genocide. Despite an inspection ordering its removal last year, it remained in place. On the night of 25 October, as citizens celebrated the Student List's historic election victory over Aleksandar Vučić’s ruling SNS party, they took the poster down themselves. Scenes like the one in Novi Sad have become the new normal in Serbia. In the weeks following the elections that ended 14 years of SNS rule, citizens have been painting over graffiti, tearing down posters, and trying to clean up the country. But all this is happening before the Student List – a one-of-a-kind grassroots movement led by students

title: AlgaeFood: When seaweed finds its way onto the plate
content:
Innovative local food production: Offer someone a piece of seaweed with a “Bon appetit!” and you are likely to be met with a degree of scepticism. Until they taste it, that is. More often than not, the next thing you hear is: “That actually tastes quite nice.”

The seaweed that grows along the Danish-German coast not only contributes to water quality, but can also be used as food – unfortunately, this happens all too rarely! Because seaweed is actually a ‘superfood’ and it is a regional resource with great potential. Depending on the species of algae, the seaweed contains protein, minerals and vitamins – and it grows in the sea without requiring agricultural land.

title: Cop31: Why the UN climate summit ended in victory for fossil fuel producing nations
content:
The UN’s annual two-week climate summit, Cop31, has ended in failure. Countries could not find consensus on a final agreement. It is the first such failure in more than 20 years.

The summit started relatively smoothly. In fact, the conference agenda was adopted within a few hours on day one, as country parties found nothing objectionable. At the time, this event looked like it might be smooth sailing: another summit simply focused on implementing policies agreed in previous years.

But week two became explosive. First, the draft agreement – which if adopted would have been known as the Antalya Accords – conceded that we have failed to keep global temperature rise below 1.5˚C and that the world is entering a period of “overshoot”. Second, oil and gas producing nations fought to keep the root cause of climate change – namely fossil fuels – out of any deal. And they succeeded, as the agreement fell through.
snippet: The UN’s annual two-week climate summit, Cop31, has ended in failure. Countries could not find consensus on a final agreement. It is the first such failure in more than 20 years.

title: How did the COP31 climate agreement fall apart – and what happens now?
content:
Two days after the COP31 global climate summit was supposed to finish, the talks in Antalya, Turkey, have come to an end – but not as we might have hoped.

Agreement simply could not be reached. The sticking point was the omission of fossil fuels in draft texts. The European Union led a revolt, shattering the consensus needed to adopt the cover text proposed by the Turkish and Australian conveners.

In a year of unprecedented climate disasters, a supercharged El Niño and as the world heads inevitably past 1.5 °C of warming, the EU and other nations said that the international process did not meet the moment.

Some coverage has suggested the rejection of the cover text is a sign the entire summit was a failure. This isn’t quite right.

These texts have always been add-ons to the formal negotiation process. Countries have regularly agreed these political, overarching statements, particularly since the Glasgow meeting in 2021, but they are not a requirement.

Its failure does not signal the end of the COP process – or the breakdown of the Paris Agreement. What it may mean is that international climate cooperation will look different from this point onwards.
snippet: Two days after the COP31 global climate summit was supposed to finish, the talks in Antalya, Turkey, have come to an end – but not as we might have hoped.
creator: Jacqueline Peel, Professor of Law, The University of Melbourne

title: “I’m not going to remove the repository”
content:
There is a hacking tool called ARTEX that is causing havoc around the world. It lets a hacker plug in their LLM of choice, and ARTEX will then spin up a bunch of AI subagents focused on different aspects of hacking, such as scoping out a target or stealing data. This tool can complete an entire hack of a target in just a few hours. The original author of ARTEX took down the tool in October after it became clear that bad people were using it. But, as I write below, ARTEX is free. Several people are still distributing it on GitHub. I spoke to them about it, asked them why, and for their thoughts about requests to take the tool down. 

And as I’m writing this, NVIDIA just said it has reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO, and Board Director. Hahahahahahahahahha.

title: French Bill Risks Deepening Police Impunity
content:
The French Senate on November 20 approved a controversial bill that risks deepening impunity for use of lethal force by police. 

The bill introduces a legal presumption of self-defense for law enforcement officers using firearms during the exercise of their duties, unless victims or their families can establish the use of lethal force was unlawful.

Because victims’ families lack access to key evidence to assess the legality of police-caused death, placing the burden of proof on them is likely to deepen impunity and seriously jeopardize pathways for accountability where lethal force was unlawful, unnecessary, or disproportionate. This is inconsistent with France’s human rights obligations with respect to protecting the right to life and use of force by law enforcement. 

The use of lethal force by police is a major concern in France. In 2023, a police officer fatally shot 17-year-old Nahel M., a racialized boy, during a traffic stop, triggering widespread scrutiny of police use of firearms.

title: Maailma tietää jo, mitä pitäisi tehdä – miksi se ei tee sitä?
content:
Antalyan ilmastokokous oli ensimmäinen sen jälkeen, kun YK:n ympäristöohjelma vahvisti, että maapallon lämpeneminen ylittää 1,5 asteen rajan. Silti lähes 200 maan neuvottelut päättyivät tuloksettomina juuri niissä kysymyksissä, jotka ovat ilmastonmuutoksen hillinnän kannalta keskeisimpiä.

Saudi-Arabia ja muut suuret öljyn- ja kaasuntuottajat vastustivat fossiilikirjauksia, ja torstaina julkaistusta päätösluonnoksesta ne putosivat pois. Dubaissa vuonna 2023 maailman maat sopivat ensimmäistä kertaa siirtymisestä pois fossiilisista polttoaineista energiajärjestelmissä. Kolme vuotta myöhemmin tätä tavoitetta ei saatu edes nimettyä Antalyan päätöslauselmaan. Tämän vuoksi EU ja useat muut maat kieltäytyivät hyväksymästä viimeistä päätösluonnosta.

Panaman ympäristöministeri Juan Carlos Navarro kuvasi tilannetta poikkeuksellisen suorasanaisesti. Hänen mukaansa "öljymafia" pitää maailman ilmastoneuvotteluja panttivankinaan.

"Olemme rakastuneet kidnappaajiimme", Navarro totesi ja vertasi valtioiden riippuvuutta fossiilisista polttoaineista Tukholman syndroomaan, jossa panttivanki alkaa tuntea kiintymystä vangitsijaansa.

title: RoboLab
content:
Seit Jahrhunderten versuchen Menschen, lebendig wirkende Maschinen zu erschaffen: von einer mechanischen Ente im Frankreich des 18. Jahrhunderts, die scheinbar Nahrung aufnehmen und verdauen konnte, bis zu einem Roboterhund im Japan der 1990er-Jahre, den man loben, tadeln und neue Tricks lehren konnte. Besonders reizvoll fanden Menschen immer, Maschinen nach ihrem Vorbild zu bauen – sogenannte Humanoide. 

Warum aber Maschinen nach menschlichem Vorbild bauen? Der menschliche Körper ist zwar leistungsfähig und anpassungsfähig, aber auch verletzlich. Andere Lebewesen haben eigene Strategien entwickelt, sich die Welt zu erschließen, und könnten uns dazu inspirieren, das Konzept „Roboter“ weiter zu fassen und bei ihrer Gestaltung über das Humanoide hinauszudenken.  

Denn wir Menschen sind mehr als unsere Körper – wir sind emotionale und soziale Wesen. Wenn wir Robotern die Fähigkeit verleihen, unsere Gesichtsausdrücke zu deuten, Gefühle nachzuahmen und kreativ zu sein, verhandeln wir dann neu, was uns als Menschen einzigartig macht?

title: West Bank: Israeli Authorities Harass, Arrest Activists Protecting Palestinian Farmers
content:
(Beirut) – Israeli authorities are detaining activists and community organizers attempting to protect Palestinian farmers during what the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) has recorded as the most violent West Bank olive harvest season in its 20 years of records, Human Rights Watch said today. 

Between October 1 and 26, 2026, OCHA recorded 397 settler attacks resulting in casualties or property damage, the highest monthly figure it has recorded since its documentation began in 2006. Israeli soldiers were present in 26.5 percent of such incidents documented by the Israeli human rights organization Yesh Din between September 27 and October 14. The Israeli military has detained hundreds of people trying to protect Palestinian farmers during their harvest, according to local media reports.

title: Israel’s destruction of Gaza has created a ‘toxic wasteland’, experts find
content:
Scientific and satellite findings warn of widespread contamination in Gaza, posing grave threats to public health ‘for generations to come’

Israel’s destruction of Gaza has left a devastating environmental legacy with poisoned water, contaminated soil and toxic air threatening the life-support systems that the population depends on for survival, according to a report.

Israel’s military assault has created widespread contamination across the entire strip, the report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (Ceobs) finds, with heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and sewage making the air, soil and water dangerous for Palestinians for decades to come.

title: pib – printable intelligent bot
content:
Werden Roboter uns ersetzen? Werden wir zu Konkurrenten? Roboter entstehen ja nicht von selbst. Erdacht, geplant und gebaut werden sie von Menschen, die darüber entscheiden, wie sie aussehen, was sie können und welchem Zweck sie dienen sollen. Doch was, wenn die Menschen hinter diesen Entscheidungen nicht jene Roboter bauen, die der gesamten Gesellschaft zugutekommen? 

Genau deshalb ist Open-Source-Technologie so wichtig, denn damit hat man die Wahl, Alternativen zu entwickeln. „Open Source“ bedeutet, dass die Baupläne einer Technologie öffentlich sind. Alle können sie als Vorlage nutzen, um sie zu erforschen, nachzubauen oder weiterzuentwickeln. Doch wer Zugang zu diesen Werkzeugen hat, trägt auch Verantwortung.  

Welchen Roboter würdest du bauen? 

Hier entsteht im Laufe der Ausstellung ein humanoider Roboter direkt vor den Augen der Besucher*innen. Alle sind eingeladen, mitzumachen und gemeinsam zu diskutieren, welche Eigenschaften Roboter haben sollten. Dabei lässt sich hautnah miterleben, wie dieses gemeinsame Vorhaben Stück für Stück Gestalt annimmt.

title: Armed Groups' Abuses Continue in Border Areas
content:
Since early November, many rural communities in the Catatumbo region, near the Colombia-Venezuela border, have suffered violent abuses and forced displacement as the 33rd Front, a dissident group of the former Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), has clashed with the National Liberation Army (ELN) over control of the territory.

During a field visit from November 9 to 12, Human Rights Watch interviewed community members, representatives of civil society organizations, humanitarian workers, and local authorities, who said these groups have continued to kill civilians, recruit children, plant antipersonnel mines, carry out drone attacks, and impose strict social control over communities.

People told us that on November 8 in Caño Salado, a rural community in Tibú, members of the 33rd Front threatened residents and accused them of collaborating with the ELN. Two community leaders were killed. “They told people to leave, or they would kill anyone who was involved with the ELN,” a civil society member told Human Rights Watch.

Dozens of families have also been displaced from Bocas de San Miguel and El Diamante, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs.

title: From first contact to lasting support: Baltic Sea Network explores youth outreach in Stockholm
content:
How can youth guidance centres reach young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET), particularly those who remain outside existing support systems? This question was at the centre of the Baltic Sea Network for Youth Guidance Centres and NEET Services meeting, held in Stockholm on 10–12 November 2026.

The City of Stockholm hosted the meeting as part of the School to Work flagship under Policy Area Education of the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR). The event brought together youth guidance practitioners, employment specialists and policymakers to exchange experiences and explore approaches to reaching young people who may not actively seek assistance.

The Stockholm meeting built on the launch of the Baltic Sea Network for Youth Guidance Centres and NEET Services in Kraków, Poland, in March 2026. During that first gathering, participants identified outreach as a key challenge for youth guidance services, highlighting the importance of finding, engaging and motivating young people who are not reached through conventional support systems.

title: Breaking the silence: Pratishta’s journey from childhood abuse to advocacy
content:
In South Asia, survivors of sexual and physical abuse are often met with judgment and stigma

Originally published on Global Voices

Editorial note: This article contains mention of gender-based violence, sexual assault, violence against children, and child sexual abuse, which may be triggering for some readers.

November 25 to December 10, 2026, marks the UN’s 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence. However, even as gender-based violence gets more recognition globally, survivors are still struggling to access social or legal justice. South Asia is no exception to this. Global Voices sat down with one survivor of childhood abuse who uses her experience to fuel her advocacy work today.

South Asia is home to nearly one quarter of the world’s population, woven with a diverse, culture-driven fabric where women are often celebrated as goddesses. However, this veneration doesn’t necessarily mean South Asian women are safe or free from abuse.

title: Arsenic in Thai Rivers Draws Scrutiny to Myanmar’s China-Linked Mining Trade
content:
By Jan Servaes

BRUSSELS | 22 November 2026 (IDN) — Arsenic detected in waterways in northern Thailand has prompted authorities to provide clean water to affected communities. Researchers traced some of the contamination to upstream gold mining in Myanmar. Reports of fish with sores in the Mekong have also raised concerns about food safety. Al Jazeera

On 16 November, the South China Morning Post reported on fish with visible sores in the Mekong. A few days earlier, environmental activist Aombun Thipsuna—chair of the Association of the Network of Community Organization Councils in the Seven Northeastern Mekong Basin Provinces—shared photos on social media of fish known locally as “pla khae,” which the local population has dubbed “zombie fish.” She told the Thai alternative news outlet Ejan that, since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, fishermen have increasingly encountered fish with such deformities.

According to Aombun, the “pla khae” can reach weights of up to 60 kg. As the fish is widely consumed in Thailand, this raises the risk of heavy metals entering the human food chain.

title: Kestävyyden materiaaliset rajat
content: Euroopan unionin ajama vihreä siirtymä on keskeinen poliittinen projekti ilmastokriisiin vastaamisessa, mutta se lisää riippuvuutta kriittisistä raaka-aineista ja kytkee EU:n entistä tiiviimmin osaksi niiden globaaleja toimitusketjuja. Vihreän siirtymän materiaalisiin edellytyksiin liittyykin monia avoimia kysymyksiä. Aiemmassa tutkimuksessa on kiinnitetty huomiota etenkin EU:n normatiivisten tavoitteiden ja käytännön politiikkatoimien välisiin jännitteisiin. Tämä katsausartikkeli esittää, että EU:n ajamaa vihreää siirtymää ja siihen linkittyvää kriittisten raaka-aineiden politiikkaa on syytä tarkastella globaalin ekstraktivismin käsitteen avulla poliittisen talouden ilmiönä, joka siirtää sosiaalisia ja ympäristöllisiä kustannuksia resursseja tuottaville alueille, kuten Kongon demokraattiseen tasavaltaan. Samalla artikkeli osoittaa myös kriittiseen realismiin tukeutuen, että vihreän siirtymän strateginen edistäminen kytkeytyy laajempiin maailmantalouden rakenteisiin, jotka ylläpitävät ja uusintavat epätasa-arvoisia valtasuhteita. Tämä haastaa käsitystä EU:n vihreästä siirtymästä yksiselitteisesti kestävänä ja oikeudenmukaisena poliittisena kehyksenä sekä korostaa tarvetta EU:n kriittisten raaka-aineiden politiikan uudelleenarviointiin.

title: Serbia and Hungary show why playing East against West may no longer pay for small European states
content:
Serbia’s student-led movement entered parliament on November 17, following its historic electoral defeat of Aleksandar Vučić’s party, after two years of protests. Seven months earlier, Hungarian voters ended Viktor Orbán’s 16 years in power.

These political transitions, following years of increasingly centralised rule, raise an economic question that extends well beyond the two countries. Can smaller peripheral states still benefit from playing competing great powers against each other?

Hungary, an EU member state, and Serbia, a long-time candidate, followed similar foreign policy strategies. Hungary called it “connectivity”; political scientists call it hedging: maintaining economic relationships with competing great powers, without fully aligning with any one of them.

In practice, both countries continued to anchor in European markets while simultaneously cultivating ties with China, Russia and the US. For years, this geopolitical balancing act seemed to offer economic opportunities and leverage well beyond their size. The countries managed to attract investment, secure energy supply and even strengthen their bargaining positions.

title: Vastarinta vai brändi? Saint Levant ja Palestiina popin valtavirrassa
content:
Saint Levant on nostanut Palestiina-kysymyksen sotaisista uutisotsikoista ja poliittisesta jargonista inhimilliselle ja ymmärrettävälle tasolle. Miksi juuri Saint Levantin kaltainen nuori, diasporassa elävä trendikäs hahmo pystyy tekemään Palestiinasta globaalisti kulutettavaa popkulttuuria? Mitä tapahtuu, kun poliittisesta identiteetistä tulee samalla vastarintaa, viihdettä ja kaupallinen brändi?

Lensin tukahduttavan kuumana elokuisena kesäpäivänä Lontooseen viettämään viikonloppua musiikkifestivaalin merkeissä. Kyseessä oli Mahrajan Festival, brittiläinen ja ensimmäistä kertaa järjestetty musiikkifestivaali Euroopassa, joka oli omistettu kokonaan arabiankieliselle musiikille. Festivaali järjestettiin Lontoon Crystal Palace Bowlissa Live Nation ja ABU Recordings toimesta. Tunnelma oli tiivis ja letkeä. Yleisössä puhuttiin lähinnä englantia ja arabiaa, ja Palestiinan liput liehuivat tapahtuma-alueen jokaisessa nurkassa. Lisäksi keffiyeh-huivit ja perinteiset Lähi-idässä käytetyt ruudulliset päähineet – joista erityisesti mustavalkoisesta versiosta on tullut palestiinalaisen identiteetin ja solidaarisuuden symboli – tuntuivat olevan festivaalin epävirallinen asukoodi.

title: Australia’s Sanctions on West Bank Settlers Increase Pressure
content:
Australia announced on November 18 further targeted sanctions on three individuals and four entities involved in illegal settlement expansion and human rights abuses against Palestinians in the West Bank. Although these sanctions are a welcome step, they are long overdue and don’t go far enough. 

The situation in the West Bank is dire. State-backed settler violence has risen to all-time highs. Tens of thousands of Palestinians have been displaced and 1,394 killed by settlers or soldiers in the West Bank since the start of 2023. The number of illegal Israeli settlements has nearly doubled, including the E1 settlement project, which even Israel’s allies have called a “red line,” and which Israeli ministers openly boast is intended to erase any possibility of a future Palestinian state. 

On the same day as Australia’s announcement, the United Kingdom announced sanctions against eight construction companies and property development firms that have not, until now, been sanctioned by any government. The individuals and companies sanctioned by Australia, however, have previously been sanctioned by the United Kingdom and other states.

title: Global left rallies in Paris to make ‘not so radical’ case for taxing billionaires
content:
PARIS — The left wants voters to know there is nothing radical about taxing billionaires.

“Radical would be cutting their heads off. But we are not proposing that,” former Chilean President Gabriel Boric told a summit against “international oligarchy” in Paris on Saturday. A minimum tax on the world’s largest fortunes, he said, is “arithmetic.”

Boric was among the left-wing politicians, union leaders and economists brought together by French economist Gabriel Zucman at the Théâtre de la Concorde, a city-owned venue within sight of the U.S. embassy and a short walk from the Elysée. 

The gathering drew lawmakers from the U.S. Congress and opposition leaders from Italy, Germany, Britain and the Netherlands, united in the belief that taxing the super-rich could help the left regain the political initiative.

Their pitch was that Zucman’s proposed annual minimum tax of 2% on billionaires’ wealth is a modest measure that most voters already support — and a potent answer to the far right.

“It’s the status quo which is radical,” said Zucman, who cites polls that put support for his tax in France at 86%.

title: Dein erster Congress? Die Chaospat:innen sind für dich auf dem 40C3 da!
content:
Interessierte Mentor:innen und Mentees können sich bis zum 30. November 2026 um 23:59 Uhr UTC+1 auf unserer Chaospat:innen-Plattform registrieren.

Auch in diesem Jahr sind die Chaospat:innen wieder beim Chaos Communication Congress am Start – und dieses Jahr ist alles ein bisschen aufregender: Wir ziehen auf ein neues Gelände! Das bedeutet auch für uns als erfahrene Pat:innen, dass wir erst einmal die Lage peilen, neue Abkürzungen entdecken und herausfinden müssen, wo es den besten Mate-Nachschub gibt. Kurzum: Es ist die perfekte Gelegenheit, diesen neuen Ort gemeinsam mit dir zu erkunden und zu unserem eigenen zu machen!

Aber keine Sorge: Auch wenn die Raumpläne für uns alle neu sind, bleiben wir natürlich deine verlässlichen Expert:innen für alles, was den Congress im Kern ausmacht. Wir wissen, wie man den überwältigenden Fahrplan bändigt, wie die Community tickt und wie man sich im kreativen Trubel nicht selbst verliert. Das Prinzip „Chaos“ haben wir schließlich längst gemeistert – die neuen Flure schaffen wir zusammen mit links.

Wir freuen uns auf viele neue Menschen, die zum ersten Mal das bunte, faszinierende Chaos auf dem Congress erleben wollen – vielleicht ja auch mit dir!

title: Australia: Use Vietnam Dialogue to Press for Rights Reforms
content:
(Sydney) – Australian officials should press the Vietnamese government to release political prisoners and reverse its intensifying repression of human rights during the upcoming 21st Australia-Vietnam Human Rights Dialogue, Human Rights Watch said today. The case of an Australian national Tran Hiep, a democracy and human rights activist, is of particular concern. He has been detained in Vietnam since he was reported missing in Cambodia in September 2026. 

Human Rights Watch urged Australia, in a submission to the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, to seek clear, concrete, and measurable progress from Vietnam on issues including political prisoners, labor rights, transnational repression, and freedom of religion and belief.

“Since Australia’s last dialogue, Vietnam has sharply intensified human rights abuses both inside and outside the country,” said Daniela Gavshon, Australia director at Human Rights Watch. “Australia needs to make it clear to Vietnam that merely holding another meeting is not itself a measure of progress.”

title: What comes after networked authoritarianism?
content:
October’s Spotlight contributors illuminated a range of political, economic, and geographic contexts

Originally published on Global Voices Advox

Image by Gerd Altmann on Pixabay.

Fifteen years ago I wrote an article about “networked authoritarianism,” describing China as “exhibit A” for how an authoritarian state adapts to the internet and then adapts digital technologies to increase its own power. I sought to counter prevailing narratives of the time that the internet and tech companies were intrinsically a liberating, democratizing force. While such narratives were eventually discredited, we must not give up on our ability to use technology to defend and exercise our rights. Nor can we simply demand that governments and companies solve the problems they jointly continue to create.

October’s spotlight on Big Tech and Authoritarianism explored a range of relationships between tech companies and political actors across the global majority. Power is wielded through digital technologies in many ways. There are no quick fixes or easy solutions to stop abuses.

title: Why Is the World Still Counting on Unproven Carbon Capture Technology?
content:
You see the promise on airline booking screens, shipping boxes, electronics and grocery aisles: “Carbon neutral.” “Net zero.” “Climate pledge friendly.” Those labels rest on the comforting premise that even when companies and countries keep burning fossil fuels, the resulting pollution can be canceled out by simply capturing the carbon and locking it away.

Recently, along with my colleagues at ProPublica and Drilled, I investigated how the world came to rely so heavily on this premise, particularly in the technology known as carbon capture and storage. CCS aims to trap carbon dioxide that would otherwise be warming the atmosphere and pump it thousands of feet below Earth’s surface, where, ideally, it stays put. The oil industry has long favored the idea. 

At the industry’s prodding, the United Nations has effectively endorsed the idea that the technology can work at a massive scale.

title: Growing up displaced in Cameroon after ten years of conflict
content:
Over 223,700 children have dropped out of school in Cameroon’s Northwest and Southwest regions, while 2,463 schools are non-operational

Originally published on Global Voices

A general view of Buea's OIC Market in the Southwest Region of Cameroon, where displaced families sell goods to support their livelihoods. Photo by Cynthia Ebot Takang. Used with permission.

For children displaced by Cameroon’s ongoing armed Anglophone conflict, reaching safety has not ended the struggle. In Buea, the capital of Cameroon’s Southwest region, some children are balancing school with market trading to help their families survive.

“At least here in Buea, there are no gunshots, and we do not have to hide in the bush,” says 11-year-old Lorane in an interview with Global Voices, describing the relative safety his family found after fleeing their home in Cameroon’s conflict-affected Southwest Region.

title: Why fossil fuel-producing countries are stalling this crucial climate report
content:
After a year of record-breaking weather and a “super” El Niño underway, there’s no doubt climate extremes are wreaking havoc across the globe.

For decades, scientists have warned us this would happen. Their research made the case for reducing fossil fuel dependence. And we’ve relied on their expertise to assess the severity and extent of climate change.

But a small bloc of fossil fuel-producing countries is now obstructing the publication of a key scientific report from the world’s leading body of climate scientists, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).

This threatens global cooperation on tackling the climate crisis. And it has created deep concern at the COP31 climate summit, currently in its final hours in Turkey, also known as Türkiye.

First, it helps to understand why this report is so significant. The IPCC is the UN body for assessing the science related to climate change. Established in 1988, it provides political leaders with independent scientific assessments on climate change and strategies for response.

title: Suomen arktinen politiikka uuteen uskoon
content:
Mitä Suomen arktisen politiikan pitäisi olla?

Arktinen alue on muuttunut maailmanpolitiikan hipihiljaisesta takapihasta polttopisteeksi.

Uusi kylmä sota Venäjän kanssa, Yhdysvaltain öykkäröinti, Kiinan kiinnostus, uudet kuljetusreitit, kriittiset mineraalit, datakaapelit ja niin edelleen. Geopoliittisen pelin kyljessä kolonialismisyytöksiä ja arktisen ympäristön hävitys.

Kaiken tämän keskellä EU julkaisi ensimmäisen arktisen strategiansa. Nyt maapallon laki on Brysselistä katsottuna pohjoista naapurustoa eikä mikä tahansa tuolla jossain. 

Samaan aikaan Suomen arktinen strategia täyttää pian jo viisi vuotta. Sen toimeenpano on jäissä, Arktinen valtuuskunta on käytännössä lakkautettu ja ministeriöissä huomio siirretty toisaalle.

Tässä jaksossa kysytään, mitä Suomen arktisen politiikan pitäisi olla. 

Aiheesta keskustelemassa juontajien Sanni Granqvistin ja Olli Puumalaisen kanssa ulkoministeriön arktinen suurlähettiläs Kalle Kankaanpää sekä Tromssan yliopiston geopolitiikan, rauhan ja turvallisuuden tutkimuskeskuksen johtaja Johanna Ikävalko.

title: Effort to regulate ‘killer robots’ delayed to 2028
content:
U.N. talks on regulating AI-powered killer robots ended without a negotiating mandate Saturday, as countries decided to extend discussions until 2028.

It’s a result that NGOs called “disappointing.”

Countries party to the U.N.’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons spent five days in Geneva trying to reach an accord to elaborate legally binding rules for weapons that can select and attack targets without human approval.

But resistance from several countries, and especially Russia, blocked those efforts. In the end, the 128 member countries agreed to launch “the elaboration of an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems,” over the next two years, Julien Thöni, the Swiss diplomat who chaired the talks, told reporters.

The issue is of growing importance as AI gains new capabilities and autonomous systems become increasingly powerful. Ukraine, Russia, Israel and others are using drones and robots in warfare, although they insist that humans still have ultimate control over pulling the trigger.

However, Stop Killer Robots, a global coalition of more than 300 organizations, said such systems have already been tested or deployed, including in Ukraine and Gaza.

SLS delar årligen ut Fredrik Pacius-priset ur Fredrik Pacius minnesfond. Priset på 20 000 euro tilldelas en person som främjat Finlands musikliv i Fredrik Pacius anda, vilket syftar på gränsöverskridande, innovativ, professionell samt kunskapsbyggande och -spridande verksamhet. Priset utdelas nu för nionde gången.

Anna-Maria Helsing är chefsdirigent för BBC Concert Orchestra och Vasa stadsorkester samt konstnärlig ledare för kammarmusikfestivalen Rusk i Jakobstad. Åren 2004–2007 studerade hon orkesterdirigering under Leif Segerstam vid Sibelius-Akademin.

Efter att 2010–2013 varit konstnärlig ledare för Uleåborgs symfoniorkester, som den första kvinnan med en sådan position i Finland, har Helsing hunnit dirigera alla större nordiska orkestrar och arbetat med många europeiska, däribland BBC Philharmonic Orchestra, Royal Scottish National Orchestra, Estniska nationalorkestern, Barcelonas symfoniorkester och Budapest Festival Orchestra.

title: Miksi toimeentulon tukeminen on tärkeää perheiden tulevaisuudelle?
content:
Toimeentulon tukeminen on tärkeää perheiden tulevaisuudelle, koska se luo perustan, jonka varaan kaikki muu rakentuu. Kun perheellä on vakaa toimeentulo, lapset voivat käydä koulua, vanhemmat voivat tehdä suunnitelmia ja yhteisö voi kehittyä. Pelkkä hätäapu ratkaisee akuutin kriisin, mutta kestävä toimeentulo rakentaa tulevaisuuden. Tässä artikkelissa käymme läpi tärkeimmät kysymykset siitä, miksi toimeentulon tukeminen on yksi tehokkaimmista tavoista auttaa perheitä maailman haavoittuvimmissa paikoissa.

Toimeentulon tukeminen tarkoittaa käytännössä toimia, joiden avulla ihmiset voivat hankkia riittävän elannon itselleen ja perheelleen kestävällä tavalla. Se ei tarkoita pelkkää rahallista avustusta, vaan kokonaisvaltaista tukea, joka voi sisältää ammattikoulutusta, pienlainoja, maatalouden kehittämistä tai yrittäjyyden tukemista.

Toimeentulon tukeminen rakentuu useista toisiaan täydentävistä elementeistä:

  • Taitojen kehittäminen: Ammatillinen koulutus ja osaamisen vahvistaminen, jotta ihmiset voivat työllistyä tai perustaa oman yrityksen
  • Taloudellinen omaehtoisuus: Pienlainat, säästöryhmät ja muut rahoitusvälineet, jotka mahdollistavat oman elinkeinon rakentamisen

title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
content:
Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’

Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections.

Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.

title: Reclaiming Indigenous culinary histories in Nepal
content:
The dominant Nepali food narrative overlooks the diverse regional histories and culinary traditions of Indigenous communities

Originally published on Global Voices

Timu khole, wild mushroom soup. Photo by Binti Gurung. Used with permission.

Food enriches our soul. It makes us who we are. However, the emergence of cosmopolitanism and global and local food politics has sidelined Indigenous food, not to mention the traditions and rituals associated with them.

“Over the last decades, ever since the country was opened up to the outside world in the 1950s, in search of a national food identity, the staple daal bhaat, a nutrient-dense combination of lentils and rice accompanied by vegetables, has been elevated to Nepal’s national dish,” writes Binti Gurung, a food historian and founder of Natural Roots Foundation, an organization dedicated to documenting, preserving, and promoting Indigenous Himalayan food heritage, traditional recipes, and local knowledge in Nepal. “The national food narrative that is being set completely obscures the varied regional histories and food practices of the Indigenous peoples.”

title: Costa cuts proposed EU budget by €44B
content:
BRUSSELS — António Costa aims to shave another €44 billion off the EU’s planned seven-year budget, according to a fresh set of numbers unveiled on Saturday.

For the first time since the budget negotiations began last year, EU regional spending, known as cohesion policy, is a target for reductions. The European Council president proposed reducing it by €8 billion compared with the last proposal, while farmers’ subsidies remained untouched.

This is a major setback for a coalition of 17 countries from Eastern and Southern Europe — including Poland, Italy and Spain — who rejected potential cuts to cohesion policy only a few days ago. However, the plan was welcomed as “a first step” by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who urged further cuts.

“This proposal is fit for tackling the challenges we are facing in our societies, and gives the European Union the necessary capacity to act,” Costa said on Saturday morning.

Research articles and research reports, to be submitted in English or German, are subject to a double-blind peer-review. The journal is based at the Research Centre for Provenance Research, Art and Cultural Property Law at the University of Bonn and at the Leipzig Museum of Fine Arts. transfer receives funding from the German Research Foundation (DFG). title: U.K. Seizes $72 Million Tied to Singapore Scandal, Drawing Scrutiny Over Early Deals
content:
Britain’s National Crime Agency has seized more than $70 million in properties tied to Singapore’s $2.3 billion money-laundering scandal, an outcome which, although hailed as a success in combating financial crime, has been criticized by an expert as a “missed opportunity” for the larger recoveries and greater accountability that a trial would likely have brought.

The NCA named last week Su Haijin and Xu Haika as two individuals “linked to an international money laundering network that had agreed to hand over around £55 million ($72.1 million) in assets after being pursued by the NCA”, in a settlement that was approved by the U.K. High Court.

OCCRP has reported extensively on the U.K. and global asset portfolio of both men, including Su Haijin’s purchase of a townhouse on Oxford Street, and Xu Haika’s purchases of multiple luxury apartments further down the same bustling high street. 

“These settlements are in the public interest, avoiding protracted and costly High Court litigation while enabling our resources to be redirected towards new investigations," said Gareth Jones, Branch Commander for Asset Denial at the National Crime Agency.

title: Neuro-inclusive Digital Citizen Science: What Does It Take?
content:
We are happy to share that our new study, Framework for Neuro-inclusive Digital Citizen Science: Results From the Neuro(Minorities)Science Collaboration, has been published in Citizen Science: Theory and Practice. This is an open access publication, meaning you do not need to register or pay to read it.

The framework was created to make digital citizen science (DCS) platforms like Zooniverse, iNaturalist, the European Citizen Science Platform, CitSci and SciStarter more accessible for neurodivergent people. It contains 91 accessibility recommendations for platform teams, research project teams and science communicators.

This publication is the result of a collaboration between 89 neurodivergent citizen scientists and allies from around the world, led by Dr Alisa Apreleva (Zooniverse Communications Lead, University of Oxford).

title: ITU Shatters Glass Ceiling
content:
It’s a momentous breakthrough: in a stunning upset, Estonia’s Nele Leosk unseated incumbent Zimbabwe’s Cosmas Zavazava in the election to become the Director of the ITU’s Development Bureau. Leosk joins re-elected American Secretary-General Doreen Bogdan-Martin, previously the only woman ever elected to an ITU leadership post. 

Beyond the gender revolution, the victories of American and Estonian women leave democratic nations in control of ITU leadership. Bahrain’s Adel Darwish (Deputy Secretary-General), Japan’s Seizo Onoe (Standardization), and France’s Eric Fournier (Radiocommunication) fill out the top team. 

Their victories are important for an open, free Internet. Despite strained transatlantic relations, Europe and the Trump Administration are cooperating in this one important international institution. Overt battles over Internet governance appear to be fading between the democracies and authoritarian Russia and China. The ITU can concentrate on the less explosive, but crucial tasks of bringing Internet access to the unconnected 26% of the global population in an affordable, sustainable fashion.

title: European Digital Infrastructure Consortium launches today to strengthen digital sovereignty in education
content:
Today, the European Commission and eight Member States are launching the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium on Education (EDU-EDIC) to pool resources and develop shared, secure and interoperable digital infrastructure and services for education.

The new consortium on education brings together Belgium, Croatia, Finland, France, Greece, Slovenia, Spain and the Netherlands, which will be hosting the EDIC.

The initiative will strengthen Europe's technological resilience while making high-quality digital tools accessible to schools, teachers and learners. It will also help narrow the digital divide in education by supporting solutions that can be used across national education systems, regardless of their resources or technological capacity. Today's launch marks an important milestone in fostering innovation and excellence in education and contributing to the EU's technological sovereignty ambitions.

Executive Vice-Presidents Henna Virkkunen and Roxana Mînzatu, together with Judith Tielen, Minister for Primary and Secondary Education of the Netherlands, will welcome the launch.

title: How much are our great-great-great-great-grandkids worth?
content: The year is 3026. One of your descendants, roughly 30 generations down the line, is heading to work. Maybe they live in a solarpunk paradise of green rooftops and take a fully electric bus. Or maybe they wake up in a sealed habitat and check the day's toxicity rating before strapping on an oxygen mask for the short walk to the underground commute, where they're safe from wildfire smoke and unpredictable storms raging above. You’ll never meet them, and after so many generations, they likely won’t even carry your DNA. But they will have inherited something from you: up to 40% of the carbon dioxide emitted today will still be in the atmosphere when they’re born. That carbon will shape the world they live in. So how do we account for the damage it will do to them? One way is to make emitting carbon cost money, which discourages pollution and raises funds for cleaner alternatives. It’s the idea behind a familiar climate slogan: “Make polluters pay.” And the bill for not cutting emissions is already here: the floods that hit the Iberian Peninsula at the beginning of the year, for example, cost €7 billion in relief payments alone. title: Taking catchment-based water management forward
content:
How can cooperation around catchment-based water management move from individual projects towards a more lasting Baltic Sea Region network?

This was the question at the heart of the Clean Water Alliances follow-up event on 11 November 2026. The online meeting continued the discussions started at the Clean Water Alliances event in Tallinn in May, bringing together catchment officers, projects, authorities and other experts to exchange experiences and consider practical next steps for cooperation across the Baltic Sea Region.

The follow-up was organised by EUSBSR Policy Areas Nutri and Hazards together with SIP LIFE WetEST, SIP LIFE ACWA and Interreg Central Baltic project BaltCOP. The programme combined practical experiences from catchment officers with discussion of the newly released BaltCOP Catchment Officer Guidebook, hazardous substances, funding and the future of pan-Baltic cooperation.

title: FCAI-X is the next AI research Flagship
content:
The Research Council of Finland has selected six centers of excellence to the Finnish Flagship Programme. Of these, Aalto University coordinates the Finnish Centre for Artificial Intelligence Excellence, FCAI-X, which develops artificial intelligence methods to support research and innovation. Lue tämä suomeksi

Product development, R&D and scientific research across fields follow the same loop: design-build-test-learn. With the assistance of AI and under human guidance, the generation of new ideas, experimentation and discovery in this loop are accelerated. FCAI-X develops the needed AI methods and collaborates with top scientists across seven scientific domains, creating new capabilities and increasing the impact of research supported by AI. FCAI-X builds on the strong foundation of AI and machine learning research of the Finnish Center for AI (FCAI), and brings the broad machine learning expertise of ELLIS Institute Finland to developing the methods and bringing them into practice and applications. 

The Flagship period of FCAI, the Finnish Center for Artificial Intelligence, is ending, but the research continues. Subscribe to the newsletter to stay up to date.

title: A Texas Police Department Got $100K After a Single Immigration Arrest. It Stands to Earn Much More.
content:
Last spring, the police chief in a tiny North Texas suburb called Pantego went before his town council with what might have sounded like an audacious pitch to bring in more money for policing.

His department could accept the federal government’s offer to get into the business of immigration enforcement. 

“I won’t say there’s unlimited funding, but there’s quite a bit of money in the fund,” Pantego Police Chief Robert Rife said during the April meeting in which council members approved an agreement with Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

He was right. After a single immigration arrest this past June, Pantego received $100,000. 

It stands to earn much more. 

Rife predicted in his presentation to the council that federal grants could bring in an additional $720,000 for the 2,500-resident town a few miles east of Fort Worth. For perspective, combined with the money it had already received, that’s roughly equivalent to 40% of the town’s $2.1 million police budget last year.

title: Research Fellow Tyyne Karjalainen earns Doctorate in Social Sciences
content:
FIIA Research Fellow, Master of Social Sciences Tyyne Karjalainen defended her dissertation in Political Science at the University of Turku on 20 November 2026. Karjalainen’s dissertation is titled “European joint agency in the context of Russia’s war in Ukraine: A role-theoretical analysis of the shifts in European security policies and the European Union’s enlargement policy”. It focuses on a fundamental dilemma in European external action: joint action is necessary, yet difficult to achieve. This dilemma became visible in the European response to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. 

Karjalainen’s dissertation applies and develops a role-theoretical framework to analyse the challenges of European joint action. It finds that

  • although the EU has collectively committed to enlargement, the process remains contested as member states, candidate countries, and external actors perform conflicting roles.

title: We sued the Pentagon again
content:
The Pentagon told a reporter that his questions would land him on its “list of people to disregard.” It’s been disregarding our Freedom of Information Act requests for the list, so this week, we sued to force it to respond. Plus, how you can fight the silencing of prison journalists, and the Trump administration tries to compel yet another reporter to reveal his sources.

Back in July, a U.S. Central Command staffer told Intercept reporter Nick Turse that his inquiries about Iranian attacks on U.S. bases across the Middle East risked putting him on an internal Defense Department “list of people to disregard.”

Naturally, Turse and Freedom of the Press Foundation (FPF) Daniel Ellsberg Chair on Government Secrecy Lauren Harper immediately filed FOIAs for the list. The Pentagon ignored the requests, so we and The Intercept sued this week to force a response.

content:

An aerial view of the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico, the largest marine oil spill in history. Under the proposed ICC amendment, oil company executives could be held accountable in such cases. Image via Wikimedia Commons. CC BY-SA 2.0.

This post is part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “Justice as infrastructure.” In this Spotlight, Global Voices is partnering with The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law (HiiL) to highlight the ways justice functions as critical infrastructure for any society. You can support this coverage by donating here.

In September 2024, Vanuatu, Fiji, and Samoa filed an amendment request at the International Criminal Court (ICC) to get “ecocide” recognized as a crime under international law. The ICC currently recognizes four criminal categories: genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and the crime of aggression.

title: OPINION: Investigate the U.S. Envoy to Syria and Iraq
content:
By David L. Phillips*

OXFORD, UK | 20 November 2026 (IDN) — Tom Barrack’s handling of U.S. policy towards Syria deserves congressional scrutiny. So do reports that he advocated a role for a business associate’s firm in a major regional oil pipeline project. The House Foreign Affairs Committee should examine whether his diplomatic responsibilities and private business relationships were adequately separated.

An investigation should establish the facts without assuming its conclusion. Questions about impartiality deserve examination even where personal financial gain has not been demonstrated.

Reuters reported in October that Barrack promoted TI Capital, founded by his business partner Ziad Ghandour, for the Kirkuk–Baniyas pipeline project. Barrack disclosed a stake in ACD-TI Oakley Investment LLC, a separate property venture managed by TI Capital. Reuters found no evidence that he would profit from the pipeline. The State Department denied that he had a financial interest or role in the project and said he complied with ethics rules. (www.jpost.com
